modules.name: Site wind climate and reference wind statistics
modules.effort: M: 6-8 person-days (ECCC/EPW parsing with calm handling, per-sector exposure transfer, two time bases, ReferenceSpec, wind rose, stability tags, data-quality badge)
modules.design_question: Which wind directions and speeds, by season and hour of use, drive pedestrian wind at this site, on a stated reference, and are the source data and exposure correction adequate?
inputs: Layer 0 georeference and true-north offset (VTC site-plan north arrow is rotated relative to the street grid)
Hourly station record (speed, direction, temperature, humidity), 30 years or more, e.g. ECCC Vancouver Intl A or Vancouver Harbour CS, or NOAA ISD; station gust kept for QA only
EPW/TMYx file (typical-year time base; wind from NOAA ISD) for solar and for the TMYx WindClimate (feeds M06)
Station metadata: anemometer height, observation sampling period (1, 2 or 10 min), terrain roughness at the station
Per-sector upwind roughness table: z0, displacement height and fetch length for each 22.5 degree sector (water versus city), drawn from a map and logged; gradient height (Toronto example 600 m)
outputs: WindClimate[concurrent-30y] and WindClimate[TMYx]: hourly series (speed, direction, season tag, comfort-hour flag, stability tag, concurrent temperature and humidity), each with a record id and its own ReferenceSpec

ReferenceSpec (one per WindClimate): z_ref (default 120 m), per-sector z0 table, displacement and gradient height, profile law, sampling period, direction reference (true north), transfer model and version
WindRoseTable: 16 sectors x speed bins x season, plus a separate calm class
NorthOffset (degrees)
DataQualityBadge (record length, completeness, exposure mismatch, calm share, sampling period declared)

parameters.name: Hourly wind record length
parameters.relationship: Longer record (30 years minimum in Toronto and Hamilton; RWDI Cambridge used 20) -> steadier frequencies of rare events like the 0.1% safety gust (about 9 h/yr) -> more reliable pass/fail. Sensitivity not quantified.

parameters.name: Comfort hours and season split
parameters.relationship: Comfort uses 06:00-23:00 winds in Toronto, Hamilton and RWDI, safety 24 h; City of London states no hours window and reports worst season plus June-August. Fewer seasons hide storm-season exceedances that annual averages smooth out.

parameters.name: Per-sector upwind roughness (fetch)
parameters.relationship: Fetch differs by sector: some cross Burrard Inlet, English Bay or False Creek, others dense city (Eddy3D: terrain the wind crosses upwind). One z0 biases sectors in opposite directions and mis-sets the flow reaching 244-305 m tower height.

parameters.name: Transfer model and gradient height
parameters.relationship: Toronto scales terrain-corrected data to gradient height (600 m example) with established models; City of London uses ESDU 01008 with Harris-Deaves profiles and a 120 m reference. An uncapped log law keeps rising above gradient height and overstates tower-top speed.

parameters.name: Reference height (ReferenceSpec)
parameters.relationship: City of London scale factors run from 0.96 (100 m) to 1.48 (600 m) for one climate, normalised at 120 m. A reference mismatch with the VAF scales every probe speed and shifts comfort classes; default 120 m, at least 100 m.

parameters.name: Observation sampling period (metadata only)
parameters.relationship: ECCC hourly speed is one sampled 1-, 2- or 10-minute mean (2-minute at aviation stations since the late 1980s). A sample estimates the hourly mean without bias, only with extra scatter, so no multiplicative factor is applied; the period is logged.

parameters.name: True-north offset of the site plan
parameters.relationship: ECCC directions are true north, so only the site-plan rotation needs correcting. A wrong offset assigns wind to the wrong facade by the same angle, shifting where downwash and corner flows are predicted.

parameters.name: Time-base concurrency
parameters.relationship: Temperature, humidity and wind from one record keep cold-and-windy hours together for M06; mixing a typical-year file with a 30-year wind record scrambles them, so M01 emits one WindClimate per time base. Logical rule, no source.

parameters.name: Calms and atmospheric stability
parameters.relationship: ECCC codes calm as direction 0, which would inflate the north sector if binned. Stable hours (Arctic outflow, clear nights) and sea breezes break neutral transfer and neutral CFD, so their share is reported separately.

metrics.name: Hourly record length
metrics.good: >= 30 years of hourly data
metrics.bad: < 30 years
metrics.method: Count years with adequate hourly coverage
metrics.basis: Toronto ToR 6.4.4 and Hamilton 2026 both specify at least 30 years of hourly data; the RWDI Cambridge report used 1995-2015, so 30 years is a municipal rule, not universal

metrics.name: Season and hour convention declared
metrics.good: Declared set: Toronto four seasons; Hamilton and RWDI two (May-Oct, Nov-Apr); City of London worst season plus Jun-Aug; comfort 06:00-23:00 for Toronto, Hamilton and RWDI; City Lawson 24 h (no hours window stated); safety 24 h
metrics.bad: Annual-only statistics, all-hours comfort for a 06:00-23:00 family, or 06:00-23:00 imposed on the City Lawson set
metrics.method: Check run configuration against the selected CriteriaSet
metrics.basis: Toronto 5.3 and 6.4.4; Hamilton technical requirement 3; RWDI Cambridge report; City of London results section (seasons, no hours window)

metrics.name: ReferenceSpec completeness
metrics.good: z_ref (default 120 m, at least 100 m), per-sector z0 and fetch, displacement and gradient height, profile law, sampling period and direction reference declared; transfer model and version logged
metrics.bad: Any field missing, a single z0 for all sectors, or station speed used as site speed
metrics.method: Schema check on each WindClimate before release to M03-M06
metrics.basis: Toronto 6.4.4 requires terrain-corrected data scaled to gradient height; City of London wants a stated reference ideally above 100 m, a climate scaled to 120 m and ESDU 01008 corrections. The 120 m default is London's convention applied to Vancouver

metrics.name: Per-sector exposure table
metrics.good: Roughness, displacement and fetch length per 22.5 degree sector from a map, water sectors separated from city sectors, transfer model named
metrics.bad: One z0 for all sectors
metrics.method: Draw upwind fetch polygons per sector on the site map; assign a Revised Davenport class (0.0002-2 m range in the Eddy3D docs) and log it; run the named transfer per sector
metrics.basis: Eddy3D defines terrain as what the wind crosses upwind; City of London names ESDU 01008. The per-sector rule is a design choice and no Vancouver roughness values were found

metrics.name: Sampling period declared, no mean-level conversion
metrics.good: Sampling period (1, 2 or 10 min) logged from metadata; sampled speeds used as hourly-mean estimates; no multiplicative conversion
metrics.bad: A gust-factor or averaging-time factor applied to station means, or station gust used for pedestrian statistics
metrics.method: Read the period from station metadata (aviation stations: 2 min since the late 1980s, 1 min before); log only
metrics.basis: ECCC glossary and technical documentation define one sampled mean ending at the observation; Toronto and Hamilton ask for hourly data with no conversion; the earlier 'inflated exceedances' claim is corrected

metrics.name: Station representativeness
metrics.good: Station exposure and airshed comparable to the downtown site, with documented correction
metrics.bad: Uncorrected airport data used as site wind
metrics.method: Compare station and site roughness and distance; log the correction model; cross-check against a nearer station when one exists
metrics.basis: No sourced numeric distance or exposure limit; ECCC lists Vancouver Harbour CS (hourly year options 1976-2026) beside Vancouver Intl A, but anemometer exposure and wind coverage are not verified

metrics.name: Concurrent time base per WindClimate
metrics.good: One WindClimate per time base (concurrent-30y, TMYx), each with its record id and ReferenceSpec; temperature, humidity and wind from the same record; exposure correction applied to both
metrics.bad: Typical-year temperature with a 30-year wind record, or uncorrected EPW airport wind
metrics.method: Tag each series with record id and years; refuse to merge series with different ids; apply the per-sector transfer to the TMYx wind too
metrics.basis: Design rule for M04 and M06; TMYx wind is airport data derived from NOAA ISD; no external source

metrics.name: Calm hours handled
metrics.good: Calms (ECCC direction 0) counted in their own class and left out of the 16 sector bins; calm share on the badge
metrics.bad: Calms binned into the north sector
metrics.method: Direction code 0 with speed 0 -> calm class
metrics.basis: ECCC glossary: a direction value of zero denotes calm; technical documentation codes CALM as 00 and north as 36

metrics.name: Stability tag
metrics.good: Hours tagged with a stability proxy (hour of day, cloud, temperature); outflow-hour share reported beside the neutral statistics
metrics.bad: Neutral transfer applied silently to Arctic-outflow or clear-night hours
metrics.method: Proxy rule logged with the run; thresholds are user-editable
metrics.basis: No sourced proxy thresholds; Arctic outflow occurs 1-3 times per winter (Climate of Vancouver)

modules.method: 1) Read the 30-year hourly station record (speed, direction, temperature, humidity) and the EPW/TMYx. 2) Treat direction as true north (ECCC; tens of degrees, 0 = calm) and rotate by the Layer 0 offset; put calms in their own class. 3) Log the sampling period; apply no mean-level conversion. 4) Build the per-sector table (z0, displacement, fetch) and transfer each sector from station to the reference height (default 120 m) with a named model (Deaves-Harris/ESDU 01008, or a log law capped at gradient height), writing a ReferenceSpec. 5) Tag stability and season; bin into 16 sectors, speed classes and seasons for comfort hours and 24 h safety hours. 6) Emit one WindClimate per time base with concurrent temperature and humidity and a data-quality badge; station gust is QA only. 7) Rank seasons from the data.
visualization: Polar wind rose per season (16 sectors, stacked speed bins in km/h) with the calm share in the centre, one panel per season, true-north arrow and rotated street-grid axis overlaid

Polar bar chart of z0 per sector (log scale) over a map thumbnail, water sectors blue and city sectors grey, beside a bar chart of hours per sector above 20 km/h at z_ref per season and a season-ranking table computed from the data
Data-quality badge (green/amber/red) with a ReferenceSpec card (z_ref, per-sector z0, sampling period, transfer model, time base) linking to the Toronto and City of London clauses

modules.limits: TMY/EPW files are constructed typical years, so rare storms are under-represented. Airport anemometers differ from downtown exposure; ECCC speeds are single 1-10 minute samples and gusts are sparse peaks. Vancouver per-sector roughness values are team estimates and ESDU 01008 was not opened. Stability is tagged, not modelled. Pedestrian statistics are not the 1-in-50-year design wind of P10. The climate is stationary; no future weather files.
modules.human_judgment: Choosing the station and transfer model, drawing the per-sector fetch map, deciding whether site data or a consultant study is needed, and interpreting local Vancouver flows such as winter outflow, sea breezes and storm winds.

modules.name: Wind-study requirement and criteria selector
modules.effort: S: 4-5 person-days (rule tables, five versioned CriteriaSets, inclusion rules, precedent table, clause-linked report)
modules.design_question: Will this massing probably need a formal pedestrian wind study in Vancouver, and which comfort and safety criteria set, with its own safety limit, should the tool apply and cite?
inputs: Layer 0: maximum tower height, count of buildings at or above 20 m, site area
Context building heights from the SITE module, including approved and future towers named in the VTC brief
Program tags: entrances, seating, transit plaza, amenity terraces, cycle routes
User choice of criteria family and trigger preset
VancouverPrecedentTable: manual entries from 2-3 downtown rezoning wind reports (criteria family, station, seasons, hours, conditions), empty until a team member downloads them
outputs: StudyTriggerReport (per analog jurisdiction: Toronto 2022, Hamilton 2026, City of London 2019; clause links and document status)

CriteriaSet: versioned typed JSON (family and version, classes, speeds and units, exceedance basis, averaging as mean or GEM, comfort hours, seasons, zone-to-class map, mandatory safety criterion or explicit none, source id, status) consumed by M04 and M06
ScenarioChecklist (existing / proposed / proposed plus approved towers / demolished-site case if the existing building is over 40 m / mitigation / phasing)
ContextSpec: minimum context radius, inclusion rules and cumulative tower list for M03 and M05
PrecedentCheck: default CriteriaSet compared with the PrecedentTable once filled

parameters.name: Tower height H
parameters.relationship: Taller tower -> higher trigger level and a tunnel requirement: Toronto Area 1 over 100 m is High, Hamilton 44 m or more, City of London above 100 m needs tunnel and CFD at detailed design. VTC towers of 244-305 m exceed every analog threshold found.

parameters.name: Height relative to surrounding buildings
parameters.relationship: Hamilton requires a tunnel study when a building of 20 m or more exceeds twice its surroundings; City of London steps up to CFD and tunnel at up to 4 times average surrounding height. Taller relative to context -> stricter study.

parameters.name: Number of buildings of 20 m or more
parameters.relationship: Two or more tall buildings move Toronto projects up one trigger level and trigger a tunnel study in Hamilton; multi-tower schemes therefore face stricter study types.

parameters.name: Criteria family and exceedance basis
parameters.relationship: Toronto, Hamilton and RWDI limit GEM at 20% exceedance; City Lawson limits mean and GEM at 5%. Safety differs too: 90 km/h at 0.1% against 15 m/s at 0.022%. One family per run, never mixed.

parameters.name: Modelled context radius and cumulative scenario
parameters.relationship: Toronto asks about 350 m, Hamilton and City of London 400 m, plus influential taller buildings beyond. Larger radius and inclusion of approved towers -> truer approach flow and sheltering; the VTC brief names approved towers, so the cumulative case is required.

parameters.name: Context inclusion rules
parameters.relationship: City of London includes consented or future buildings immediately around the site at any height, and those taller than the surrounding average within 300 m, plus a demolished-site case if the existing building exceeds 40 m. Omitting them misstates sheltering.

parameters.name: Vegetation and small features in the baseline
parameters.relationship: Toronto does not consider landscaping unless agreed with the City; City of London ignores landscape under 8 m and models features projecting over 0.5 m near pedestrians. Taking planting credit in baseline runs would understate wind.

parameters.name: Higher Buildings Policy microclimate criterion
parameters.relationship: Policy criterion says a higher building should not contribute to adverse microclimate effects; it has no number, so the team must adopt numeric criteria and state why. Wording seen only in search snippets of the 2011/2018 versions.

metrics.good: Low: over 20 m and under 60 m (CFD Phase 1 and 2 only)
metrics.bad: High: over 100 m (CFD Phase 1 plus wind-tunnel study at rezoning)
metrics.method: Compare tower height and context with Toronto Table 1 and the 3.b shift rules
metrics.basis: Toronto ToR Tables 1 and 2, re-read in r1

metrics.name: Hamilton-analog trigger
metrics.good: Under 20 m: no study
metrics.bad: 44 m or more, or 20 m+ and over 2x surroundings, or 2+ buildings of 20 m+: quantitative wind-tunnel study
metrics.method: Evaluate Hamilton rules 1-3 on Layer 0
metrics.basis: Hamilton guidelines, last updated 20 Feb 2026; adoption status unconfirmed (file name says 'ph1proposed')

metrics.name: City of London-analog trigger
metrics.good: Similar to or lower than surroundings and up to 25 m: no study unless sensitive uses
metrics.bad: Above 100 m: tunnel or CFD for massing, then tunnel and CFD by independent consultants at detailed design
metrics.method: Compare height and average surrounding height with the City of London approach table
metrics.basis: City of London 2019 table of recommended approach by building height

metrics.name: Vancouver Higher Buildings Policy microclimate criterion
metrics.good: No adverse microclimate effects (qualitative)
metrics.bad: Adverse microclimate effects
metrics.method: Present as qualitative pass/flag linked to the chosen numeric criteria in M04
metrics.basis: 2011/2018 policy wording seen only in search snippets; 1997 PDF not opened (HTTP 403 again in r2, also via the Shape Your City download redirect)

metrics.name: Default criteria set for Vancouver runs
metrics.good: Toronto 2022 three-class set (10/15/20 km/h GEM at 80%), editable; Hamilton 2026 is equal or stricter at every shared class
metrics.bad: Unstated or mixed criteria
metrics.method: Preset selection stored with the run and shown in every result
metrics.basis: No Vancouver numeric criteria found. Toronto chosen as the downtown tall-building analog with an explicit High tier, a verified zone-to-class table and three classes. The attempt in r1 and r2 to obtain downtown Vancouver rezoning wind reports failed (all City of Vancouver hosts returned 403), so the default stays a team assumption until the PrecedentTable is filled by hand

metrics.good: At least two downtown Vancouver rezoning wind reports tabulated (criteria family, station, seasons, hours, mitigation conditions) and the default CriteriaSet justified from them
metrics.bad: None obtained: default remains an Ontario-analog team assumption
metrics.method: A team member downloads reports (Shape Your City or rezoning applications, manual download if bots are blocked) and fills the PrecedentTable; M02 compares family, station and hours with the default
metrics.basis: Automated fetches of vancouver.ca, guidelines.vancouver.ca, syc.vancouver.ca, council and rezoning domains returned HTTP 403; the Bay Parkade FAQ names no wind study; evidence is therefore missing, not negative

metrics.name: CriteriaSet integrity
metrics.good: Each set carries its own classes, exceedance basis, averaging, comfort hours and safety criterion (Toronto 10/15/20 km/h, 06:00-23:00; Hamilton 10/14/17/20; RWDI 6/8/10/12 mph; City Lawson 2.5/4/6/8 m/s, 24 h)
metrics.bad: A merged 'RWDI/Toronto' set, Lawson speeds at 20%, 06:00-23:00 imposed on City Lawson, or a set with no safety criterion
metrics.method: Schema validation of each CriteriaSet at load and at run
metrics.basis: Earlier spec merged Toronto's three classes with the four classes of RWDI and Hamilton; corrected after round 1. In r2 the City Lawson comfort hours changed from 06:00-23:00 to 24 h because the guideline states no hours window

metrics.name: Context radius, inclusion rules and scenario set
metrics.good: Radius at least max(400 m, about 2H) plus influential towers beyond; consented or future buildings immediately around the site at any height and those taller than the surrounding average within 300 m; scenarios existing, proposed, proposed plus approved and future towers, demolished-site if existing building over 40 m, mitigation, phasing

metrics.method: Check ContextSpec against the run; list towers added beyond the radius
metrics.basis: 350 m (Toronto) and 400 m (Hamilton, City of London) are minima with taller buildings beyond to be included; 300 m, immediate-building and 40 m rules are City of London; the 2H term is a team assumption

modules.method: Read maximum tower height, count of buildings of 20 m or more, site area and context heights from Layer 0 and the SITE module. Evaluate each analog rule set (Toronto Table 1 with +1 level shifts, Hamilton rules 1-3, City of London height bands, Barrie 6-storey trigger) and output a level per jurisdiction with clause link and document status. Custom edits become team assumptions; wrong claims stay visible as FALSE ASSUMPTION. Compare the default with the PrecedentTable once filled.

modules.name: Early massing wind-risk screening
modules.effort: M: 7-10 person-days (geometry rules, 3D flag overlay, source-linked reasons)
modules.design_question: Which massing moves (tower height, podium, step-backs, corners, tower gaps, through-block openings) are likely to create downwash, corner acceleration or channelling in the public realm?
inputs: Layer 0 footprints, heights, canopy objects and program tags (vegetation excluded from the baseline)
Context building heights within the ContextSpec radius from M02 (default max(400 m, about 2H))
WindClimate from M01 (prevailing and strong-wind sectors)
Zone tags: entrances, sidewalks, plazas, transit plaza, mid-block connections, cycle routes
outputs: WindRiskField: per-rule Low/Medium/High flags per facade segment, corner and public-space zone, with reason codes and clause links
RankedActions list (largest-scale changes first)
DirectionalExposure table (windward width and exposure height by sector)
PriorityProbes: probe points to seed M04 and M05
CanopyCoverageTable per frontage (to M06)
WindRiskIndex (0-100): computed but hidden until a CalibrationLog exists

parameters.name: Exposure height above upwind context
parameters.relationship: Tower height above the tallest upwind context (sector-weighted) -> more stream intercepted and redirected downward (downwash) onto the base; short buildings rarely cause adverse impacts. Regulatory ratio triggers such as Hamilton's 2x sit in M02.

parameters.name: Windward facade width
parameters.relationship: Wider windward face -> larger intercepted flow and stronger downwash; Hamilton states tall, wide facades are generally undesirable.

parameters.name: Podium and tower offset from podium edge
parameters.relationship: Podium with a set-back tower deflects downflow before it reaches the street, lowering pedestrian-level speed; Toronto lists tower offset change as a significant wind change. Size of the benefit is not quantified in opened sources.

parameters.name: Lower building directly upwind of the tower
parameters.relationship: A lower upwind building can enlarge downflow on the tower and accelerate wind in the gap and at windward corners, yet shorter buildings upwind of taller ones lower tower exposure. Net effect depends on gap and heights.

parameters.name: Corner geometry
parameters.relationship: Sharp corners -> flow separates and accelerates at pedestrian level; chamfered or rounded corners streamline flow, stepped or re-entrant corners diffuse it, lowering corner speeds.

parameters.name: Gap between buildings aligned with strong-wind sector
parameters.relationship: Toronto, Hamilton and RWDI describe channelling in narrow gaps, but idealised steady-RANS canyons gave larger uncomfortable zones at 2x height than at 1x. Effect depends on gap ratio and on whether the gap is a through-passage; no monotonic rule.

parameters.name: Through-block openings, underpasses, colonnades
parameters.relationship: Passages can accelerate flow along mid-block connections, yet passage studies (Blocken and co-authors, recalled, not opened) report wind-blocking rather than classic Venturi acceleration; colonnades also act as wind control. Effect depends on orientation and geometry.

parameters.name: Canopies, recessed entrances, covered walkways
parameters.relationship: Deep, wrap-around and corner canopies and recessed entrances intercept downwash and create sheltered waiting zones; effect is local and secondary to massing. Canopy coverage also feeds rain protection in M06.

metrics.name: Exposure height above upwind context
metrics.good: Lower than the baseline scheme in the strongest-wind sectors
metrics.bad: Higher than the baseline scheme
metrics.method: Tower top minus the highest upwind roof within the radius, weighted by sector frequency from M01
metrics.basis: Discriminates between options (regulatory height triggers sit in M02 because every VTC scheme is High); no sourced limit

metrics.name: Windward facade width by sector
metrics.good: Narrower than the baseline scheme toward strong-wind sectors
metrics.bad: Wide face toward a strong-wind sector
metrics.method: Projected facade width perpendicular to each 22.5 degree sector
metrics.basis: Direction sourced (Hamilton: tall and wide facades are generally undesirable); no numeric limit

metrics.name: Windward corner treatment
metrics.good: Chamfered, rounded, stepped or re-entrant corners
metrics.bad: Sharp corners on a tall windward volume
metrics.method: Detect corner turning angle and tag treatment
metrics.basis: Toronto 6.7.2 building-form strategies (qualitative)

metrics.name: Tower-podium offset depth
metrics.good: No sourced target; calibrate with M05 runs
metrics.bad: No sourced limit
metrics.method: Measure tower face to podium edge
metrics.basis: Direction of effect sourced, magnitude not; podium and separation literature (Tsang et al. 2012, recalled) not opened

metrics.name: Lower building within one tower height upwind
metrics.good: None within one tower height in a strong-wind sector
metrics.bad: Present within one tower height
metrics.method: Distance from tower to lower upwind buildings along each strong-wind sector
metrics.basis: Mechanism sourced (Toronto, Hamilton); the one-tower-height distance is an editable placeholder

metrics.name: Gap aligned with strong-wind sector
metrics.good: Not aligned (outside one 22.5 degree sector), or a closed-ended gap
metrics.bad: Through-passage aligned within one 22.5 degree sector of a strong-wind direction
metrics.method: Gap axis angle versus sector with strong-wind frequency from M01; tag through-passage or closed gap
metrics.basis: Editable placeholder; mechanism sourced, angle not; gap effect is non-monotonic in an idealised study (S07); the through-passage distinction rests on passage literature not opened

metrics.name: Composite wind-risk index per facade, corner and zone
metrics.good: Shown only after a CalibrationLog (at least about 10 massings with L2 runs) exists, then Low band by editable cut-off
metrics.bad: Shown on boards without calibration (false precision for a jury-facing output)
metrics.method: Weighted sum of rule flags by sector frequency; weights and cut-offs are team assumptions to be recalibrated against CFD; per-rule flags are shown until then
metrics.basis: No sourced scoring scheme and no calibration dataset exist; the count of 10 massings is a team placeholder

modules.method: For each of 16 wind sectors, weighted by seasonal strong-wind frequency from M01: (1) compute each tower's exposure height above the upwind context within the M02 radius and its windward width; (2) detect lower buildings within one tower height upwind (team assumption); (3) find gaps and passages whose axis lies within one sector of the wind, separating through-passages from closed gaps; (4) flag windward corners by turning angle and treatment (sharp, chamfer, round, step); (5) check podium offset and canopy presence at entrance and sidewalk zones. Each rule gives Low/Medium/High with a reason code and clause link. The composite 0-100 index stays hidden until calibrated against L2 runs. Regulatory height triggers sit in M02. Output priority probes for M04/M05 and a canopy-coverage table for M06.
visualization: Plan view of Layer 0 with arrows per strong-wind sector; windward corners as dots and facade segments as lines coloured Low (blue) / Medium (amber) / High (red) by the highest single rule flag
Ground-plane zone polygons shaded by flag count (0-8 rules triggered, legend shown); the composite 0-100 panel stays greyed with the label 'uncalibrated' until a CalibrationLog exists
Radar chart of the eight factors per tower
Reason-code table; each row links to the Toronto/Hamilton/RWDI clause, with a banner stating that this is screening and predicts no speeds

Numeric rule cut-offs, including the one-tower-height upwind distance, are unsourced and editable.

CriteriaSet from M02 (with comfort hours and safety criterion)
Turbulent kinetic energy or turbulence intensity per probe (required for GEM families)
outputs: ReferenceGateReport: pass, or refusal with the mismatched fields (reference, time-base tag, inflow declaration), or the logged conversion applied
ComfortMap: per probe and season, exceedance fraction, class, pass/fail against the zone requirement
SafetyFlags (indicative below L3; blocked when the CriteriaSet has no safety criterion)
ZoneComplianceTable and CyclistRouteTable
ProbeWindSeries per time base: hourly mean and GEM series at the probe, with time-base tag and ReferenceSpec, for M06

parameters.name: Reference chain (U_ref and VAF normalisation)
parameters.relationship: V_p = VAF x U_ref needs U_ref at the height, roughness and profile law that normalised the VAF, from the same time base. Eddy3D ABL defaults (10 m, z0 1 m) and City of London (above 100 m, scaled to 120 m) differ; a mismatch scales every probe speed.

parameters.name: Criteria family and exceedance basis
parameters.relationship: Lower allowed exceedance (City Lawson 5% against Toronto, Hamilton and RWDI 20%) -> stricter class for the same wind; limits are used only with their own exceedance basis, averaging, hours and safety criterion.

parameters.name: Gust treatment
parameters.relationship: GEM is the larger of mean and gust/1.85, gust = mean + 3 RMS (Eddy3D: U + g sqrt(2k/3)), so GEM exceeds the mean only where turbulence intensity exceeds about 28%. Isotropic RMS understates streamwise turbulence (recalled, about 20-40%); declare g and an anisotropy factor.

parameters.name: Zone to required class
parameters.relationship: Toronto: Sitting for seating, balconies and terraces; Standing for entrances and bus stops; Walking for sidewalks and laneways. RWDI: walking or strolling suits sidewalks. Stricter intended use -> lower tolerable speed -> more failures.

parameters.name: Number of simulated wind directions
parameters.relationship: Fewer directions -> coarser, less reliable class map. In one case 16 directions reproduced the 64-direction class over 96% of the area, 8 over 92% (called insufficient), 4 over 79%; City of London requires 36.

parameters.name: Season and governing season
parameters.relationship: The worst season sets the verdict, but which season governs Vancouver must be read from the M01 wind rose; Ontario statements about winter and spring do not transfer. Hamilton accepts some winter degradation as outdoor use falls.

parameters.name: Probe density and placement
parameters.relationship: Sparser probes can miss corner and entrance hot spots; Toronto and Hamilton expect probes about every 10 m along frontages and at least about 50 locations; City of London asks for about 3 probes at each corner.

parameters.name: Cycle routes
parameters.relationship: City of London asks at least one probe every 40 m on cycling paths around the development and applies the 15 m/s safety limit to cyclists; Toronto and Hamilton give no cyclist rule. Cross-wind gusts at building corners are the concern.

parameters.name: Time base of the series
parameters.relationship: ProbeWindSeries is built per time base from the matching WindClimate and M06 refuses mixed tags. TMYx under-represents storms, so classes from it are labelled typical-year, not 30-year statistics.

metrics.name: Reference-chain gate
metrics.good: VAF reference equals the U_ref reference, time-base tags match, inflow profile declared, or a logged conversion is applied
metrics.bad: Mismatched or missing reference, time base or inflow declaration: classification refused
metrics.method: Compare ReferenceSpec fields (z_ref, z0, profile law, averaging time, probe height) and tags
metrics.basis: City of London: reference at a height and location unaffected by the models, with scale factors 0.96-1.48; Toronto 6.4.4: terrain-corrected, gradient-height-scaled data

metrics.name: Homogeneity report present (replaces the 1.5 m empty-domain test)
metrics.good: Empty-domain run shows U, k and epsilon at the building position within the stated tolerance of the inlet profile at 1.5 m, 10 m, H/2 and H
metrics.bad: No report, or a pass claimed at 1.5 m only with z0 = 1 m
metrics.method: Read the homogeneity report from M05 or the import template; refuse if absent
metrics.basis: The earlier test (probe at 1.5 m within 5% with Eddy3D defaults) is ill-posed: 1.5 m lies in the roughness sublayer when z0 = 1 m and the standard rough wall function would need cells about 20 m high (Blocken et al. 2007, recalled); tolerances are editable

metrics.name: Seasonal comfort category (Toronto 2022, three classes)
metrics.good: GEM at or below the zone limit for at least 80% of 06:00-23:00 hours: Sitting 10, Standing 15, Walking 20 km/h
metrics.bad: GEM above 20 km/h for more than 20% of hours (Uncomfortable), or class worse than the zone requires
metrics.method: Exceedance of the hourly GEM series per season (four seasons)
metrics.basis: Toronto ToR Table 3; earlier label 'RWDI/Toronto' merged two different sets and is corrected

metrics.name: Seasonal comfort category (Hamilton 2026, four classes)
metrics.good: Sitting under 10, Standing under 14, Strolling under 17, Walking under 20 km/h at 80% occurrence, two seasons (May-Oct, Nov-Apr)
metrics.bad: Over 20 km/h (Uncomfortable)
metrics.method: As above with Hamilton limits and two seasons
metrics.basis: Hamilton Table 1, last updated 20 Feb 2026

metrics.name: Seasonal comfort category (RWDI, mph)
metrics.good: GEM at or below 6 (Sitting), 8 (Standing), 10 (Strolling), 12 mph (Walking), i.e. about 9.7/12.9/16.1/19.3 km/h, at 20% exceedance, 06:00-23:00
metrics.bad: Above 12 mph (Uncomfortable) or class worse than the zone requires
metrics.method: As above with RWDI limits; summer May-Oct, winter Nov-Apr
metrics.basis: RWDI Cambridge report criteria table; not identical to Hamilton's 14 and 17 km/h

metrics.name: Seasonal comfort category (City Lawson, London 2019)
metrics.good: Mean and GEM at or below 2.5 (Frequent Sitting), 4 (Occasional Sitting), 6 (Standing), 8 m/s (Walking) for 95% of all hours; the worse of mean and GEM governs; only the thresholds transfer, not London's climate coefficients
metrics.bad: Above 8 m/s (Uncomfortable), class worse than the zone requires, or the 06:00-23:00 window applied
metrics.method: Exceedance at the 5% level on both series over 24 h data; worst season plus June-August
metrics.basis: City of London 2019 guideline states no comfort-hours window; its Weibull coefficients are explicitly not valid for other areas. The r1 wording 'comfort hours' (06:00-23:00) is corrected

metrics.name: Lawson, Hagbo 2022 version (mean speed only)
metrics.good: Mean speed at or below 4 (Sitting), 6 (Standing), 8 (Strolling), 10 m/s (Business walking) for at most 5% of hours; comfort only
metrics.bad: Safety reported from this set, or described as a GEM set
metrics.method: Exceedance at the 5% level on mean speed
metrics.basis: Secondary source: 'a version of' Lawson, mean speed only, no safety criterion; primary Lawson text not opened

metrics.name: Safety criterion bound to the family
metrics.good: Gust over 90 km/h for no more than 0.1% of 24 h hours (about 9 h/yr) for Toronto, Hamilton, RWDI (56 mph); City Lawson 15 m/s mean and GEM at 0.022% (about 2 h/yr)
metrics.bad: Toronto safety applied to a Lawson run, or a set with no safety limit reporting safety
metrics.method: Read the safety field of the CriteriaSet; compute the annual exceedance on 24 h hours
metrics.basis: Toronto Table 3, Hamilton Table 2, RWDI 56 mph, City of London safety table

metrics.name: Low-wind flag
metrics.good: Mean speed under 5 km/h for less than 80% of hours (80% is the example value in the note)
metrics.bad: Mean speed under 5 km/h for 80% or more of hours: low air circulation, possible exhaust build-up and heat in full sun
metrics.method: Share of hours with mean speed below 5 km/h
metrics.basis: Toronto Table 3 note 3 refers to wind speeds lower than 5 km/h for the majority of the time (e.g. 80%), not to GEM; the r1 wording is corrected

metrics.name: GEM turbulence input present
metrics.good: Imported or M05 VAFField carries TKE or turbulence intensity per probe, with g (3) and an anisotropy factor in MethodMetadata; RANS-based GEM labelled indicative
metrics.bad: GEM family run on mean speed only without a warning badge (GEM silently collapses to the mean)
metrics.method: Check the turbulence field; block GEM families or apply a declared default turbulence intensity with a warning badge
metrics.basis: Eddy3D computes GEM as U + g x sqrt(2k/3); GEM exceeds the mean only above about 28% turbulence intensity by definition; the anisotropy factor has no sourced value

metrics.name: Significance of change against baseline
metrics.good: Negligible or beneficial: class unchanged or calmer
metrics.bad: Major adverse: safe becomes unsafe, or suitable becomes unsuitable
metrics.method: Delta of class per probe, existing vs proposed, rated with the City of London scheme
metrics.basis: City of London 2019 significance tables; Hamilton: improve where possible, no significant degradation, winter allowance

metrics.name: Sidewalk required class
metrics.good: Walking at least; Strolling preferred where the set has it
metrics.bad: Uncomfortable on a sidewalk, or Sitting demanded of all sidewalks
metrics.method: Zone map in the CriteriaSet
metrics.basis: RWDI says walking or strolling suits sidewalks; the earlier wording 'strolling or better' is corrected

metrics.name: Cycle-route check
metrics.good: Probe at least every 40 m along cycle routes; mean and GEM below 15 m/s at 0.022% (City Lawson safety limit, applied to cyclists)
metrics.bad: Exceedance of the safety limit at any cycling location, or no probes on cycle routes
metrics.method: Place probes along routes from Layer 0; compute the annual exceedance on 24 h data
metrics.basis: City of London: the 15 m/s safety limit applies to cyclists and tunnel probes are at least every 40 m on cycling paths; use with Toronto or Hamilton families is a team choice

metrics.name: Mixed criteria check
metrics.good: One family per run (speed limits with their own exceedance basis, averaging, hours and safety)
metrics.bad: Lawson speeds applied at 20% or RWDI speeds at 5%
metrics.method: Validate CriteriaSet consistency before classification
metrics.basis: Assumption that Lawson and RWDI limits are interchangeable is corrected: bases differ

modules.method: Gates: stop if the VAFField ReferenceSpec or time-base tag differs from the WindClimate's (unless a logged transfer applies) or if the inflow declaration and homogeneity report are missing. For each probe p and hour h: V_p(h) = VAF_p(theta_h) x U_ref(h), interpolating between the two nearest simulated directions (Eddy3D: Interpolate or Nearest). Gust = mean + g x RMS (g = 3), RMS from TKE or turbulence intensity with the declared anisotropy factor; GEM = max(mean, gust/1.85); without turbulence data GEM families are blocked or flagged. Per season and the family's hours, take the best class whose exceedance fraction is within the family's allowance (20% or 5%). Safety: share of 24 h hours above the family's limit; no safety criterion means no safety output. Compare with the zone requirement, check cycle routes, flag low-wind probes on mean speed, rate change against the existing scenario.
visualization: Four false-colour maps (one per season) on the ground plane at 1.5 m: Sitting, Standing, Walking, Uncomfortable in a colour-blind-safe sequential ramp, plus Strolling or the two Lawson sitting classes when those sets are chosen
Black hatched markers for probes violating the safety criterion, labelled indicative below L3; cycle-route probes drawn as diamonds along the route
Per-zone pass/fail badges (entrance, sidewalk, plaza, terrace, cycle route) linked to the clause that sets the limit, and a reference-chain badge (z_ref, z0, time base, averaging time)

Existing-vs-proposed delta map rated with the City of London significance scheme, and a probe table with GEM, exceedance and class; banner 'No VAFField imported: M03 screening only' when no data are loaded

libraries.role: Probe-hour arithmetic, exceedance, Weibull or empirical statistics (licences not re-verified)

libraries.name: Eddy3D Pedestrian Wind Comfort component
libraries.role: Reference implementation offering Lawson General, LDDC, 2001, Davenport and NEN 8100 classes; thresholds not stated on its page; free per its docs, source licence not stated
libraries.license: Free for all users; open-source status unresolved

libraries.name: plotly.js / three.js
libraries.role: Maps and 3D ground overlay

modules.limits: The classification is only as reliable as its input factors. Steady RANS differed from a wind tunnel by -1% to -35% in mean speed in one benchmark, and RANS turbulence gives indicative GEM only. Airport statistics are assumed spatially uniform after the per-sector transfer. High-trigger rezonings need tunnel evidence for safety. The core release has no VAF engine: without an imported VAFField the UI shows M03 screening only.
modules.human_judgment: Deciding the intended use of each space (for example Sitting at the transit plaza), accepting or arguing an exceedance, and trading wind comfort against program and public-realm goals.

modules.name: Fast wind simulation engine: CFD and surrogates
modules.effort: v1 scope: XS (1-2 days) Eddy3D/tunnel workflow guide and import template feeding M04; M (5-7 days) documented OpenFOAM-12 L2-lite case template (capped inflow, rough-wall set-up, homogeneity test) run offline. Hosted pipeline and L2-full: L (3-5 person-weeks), roadmap
modules.design_question: How should the tool produce directional velocity amplification factors for a massing quickly, on a stated reference and inflow, at what fidelity and compute cost, and how is accuracy declared?
inputs: Layer 0 mesh (STL/OBJ) of the scheme plus context to the ContextSpec radius, at least max(400 m, about 2H); features over 0.5 m near pedestrian zones modelled; vegetation excluded from baseline
Approved and future towers as a required cumulative context scenario, plus influential taller towers beyond the radius when upwind
Wind sectors and the per-sector ReferenceSpec from M01 (approach z0 per direction, gradient height)
ProbeSet and priority probes from M03
Inflow profile choice (Deaves-Harris/ESDU or log law capped at gradient height) and top boundary type
Fidelity level selected by the user
outputs: VAFField: probe x direction speed ratios with ReferenceSpec (reference height, approach z0, profile law, gradient height, probe height), inflow declaration up to at least 1.2 H, top boundary type, optionally turbulent kinetic energy

MethodMetadata: code and version, mesh and cell count, turbulence model, wall treatment, domain size in H and blockage ratio, homogeneity report, core-hours, validation case, fidelity label, uncertainty tag
FlowViz meshes: streamlines, vertical slices

parameters.name: Proximity model radius
parameters.relationship: Toronto asks about 350 m, Hamilton and City of London 400 m, plus influential taller buildings beyond. That is only about 1.1-1.6 tower heights for 244-305 m towers; a larger radius capturing upwind towers -> truer approach flow and wakes.

parameters.name: Domain size relative to H
parameters.relationship: AIJ practice as reported: 6 Hmax high (5 above the tallest building), 15 Hmax downstream, blockage at most 3%; Hagbo used 6 H and 15 H. At H = 305 m that is about 1.8 km high and 6 km long. Smaller domains raise blockage, so it is logged.

parameters.name: Number of wind directions
parameters.relationship: Toronto requires at least 16 for CFD and 36 for tunnel; City of London 36 for all studies; Hamilton CFD may use prevailing directions only, weighted over all directions. Fewer directions -> coarser classes (79% same class with 4, 96% with 16, by area, one case).

parameters.name: Turbulence model and steadiness
parameters.relationship: Steady RANS tends to overpredict high-speed areas and underpredict wakes against a tunnel; Toronto accepts two-equation RANS or LES; City of London avoids standard k-epsilon, calls realisable k-epsilon the robust standard and allows k-omega SST on a suitable mesh.

parameters.name: Mesh and probe height
parameters.relationship: City of London asks 0.3 m cells near entrances and corners, 10 cells across a canyon, 3 prism layers below 1.5 m and modelled features over 0.5 m near pedestrians; Toronto ignores under 1 m. Coarser near-ground mesh -> poorer 1.5 m speeds.

parameters.name: Reference and inflow profile
parameters.relationship: VAF depends on where U_ref is defined: Eddy3D ABL defaults to 10 m, 5 m/s and z0 1 m with a log law; City of London wants a reference above 100 m clear of the model. OpenFOAM-12 atmBoundaryLayer is an uncapped log law.

parameters.name: Inflow profile cap and top boundary
parameters.relationship: Tower-top speed drives downwash, so inflow must stay physical to about 1.2 H: capped at gradient height (Deaves-Harris/ESDU, or power law to z_g then constant) with a consistent top condition. Hagbo used a log law with a slip top.

parameters.name: Ground roughness and wall function
parameters.relationship: A standard rough wall function turns z0 = 1 m into a sand-grain height near 20 m (Blocken 2007, recalled), incompatible with 0.3 m cells. Use an atmospheric rough wall function for the approach fetch and a small z0 where buildings are explicit.

parameters.name: Fidelity level
parameters.relationship: Rules (M03) -> ML surrogate -> RANS lite -> RANS full -> wind tunnel: gust reliability rises, speed falls. Surrogate vendors claim seconds to minutes; independent accuracy for supertall downtown contexts is not verified.

parameters.name: Compute budget
parameters.relationship: One steady k-omega SST case took 15 h on one 2018 core for 0.26 M cells, about 57 core-hours per million cells. Linear scaling: 2-5 M cells x 16 directions is roughly 1,800-4,600 core-hours; a lower bound.

parameters.name: Context scenario
parameters.relationship: Existing plus approved towers change upwind sheltering and channelling; Toronto models projects approved in the last 5 years, City of London consented schemes, Hamilton future cases only if warranted. The VTC brief names future approved towers, so the cumulative case is required.

metrics.name: Directions simulated
metrics.good: At least 16 equal sectors for CFD (Toronto); 36 for tunnel (Toronto, Hamilton) and for any City of London study
metrics.bad: Fewer than 16 for CFD; Hamilton's prevailing-only CFD is accepted by Hamilton but fails Toronto
metrics.method: Check run metadata
metrics.basis: Toronto 6.4.2 and 6.4.3; Hamilton Technical Requirement 1.A allows prevailing directions for qualitative CFD and 1.B requires 36 for tunnel; City of London 36. The earlier claim that both cities require 16 CFD directions is corrected

metrics.name: Modelled context radius
metrics.good: At least max(400 m, about 2H) plus influential towers beyond it
metrics.bad: 350 m or less, or no upwind towers beyond the radius
metrics.method: Measure from site boundary to the domain context edge; list added towers
metrics.basis: Toronto 6.4.1: 350 m is a minimum and tall buildings outside it that could influence the site must be included; Hamilton and City of London 400 m; the 2H term is a team assumption

metrics.name: ReferenceSpec on the VAFField
metrics.good: Reference height, approach z0, profile law and probe height declared
metrics.bad: Reference missing: M04 refuses the field
metrics.method: Schema check on the VAFField
metrics.basis: City of London requires a stated reference; Eddy3D's VAF page names no reference height, so users must copy their ABL settings

metrics.name: Inflow profile and top boundary declared
metrics.good: Profile capped at gradient height and declared up to at least 1.2 H; top condition consistent with it (prescribed shear stress or fixed U, k, epsilon, per Richards and Hoxey, recalled)
metrics.bad: Uncapped log law to the domain top with an undeclared top condition, or a profile declared only near the ground
metrics.method: Read the inlet files and compare the profile at 1.2 H with the declared law; refuse the VAFField if absent
metrics.basis: OpenFOAM-12 atmBoundaryLayer is an uncapped log law; City of London names Harris-Deaves/ESDU 01008; Hagbo used a slip top; 1.2 H and the Richards-Hoxey top condition are team and recalled choices

metrics.name: Horizontal homogeneity of the empty domain
metrics.good: U, k and epsilon at the building position within the stated tolerance of the inlet profile at 1.5 m, 10 m, H/2 and H (placeholder 5% on U)
metrics.bad: Profile decays along the domain, or a pass shown only at 1.5 m
metrics.method: Run the domain without buildings and compare profiles at the future building position with the inlet
metrics.basis: Replaces the 1.5 m empty-domain test; Blocken et al. 2007 on wall-function inhomogeneity (recalled, not opened); tolerance is a team placeholder

metrics.name: Ground roughness and wall-function consistency
metrics.good: Approach ground uses an atmospheric rough wall function (nutkAtmRoughWallFunction) with z0 equal to the inlet z0; wall-adjacent cell centre above the equivalent sand-grain height or the exception logged; small z0 (placeholder 0.01-0.05 m) on explicitly modelled ground
metrics.bad: z0 = 1 m on a ground with 0.3 m cells, or the same large z0 counted again where buildings are explicit
metrics.method: Inspect boundary-condition files and first-cell heights
metrics.basis: nutkAtmRoughWallFunction exists in OpenFOAM-12 and is meant for use with atmBoundaryLayerInletVelocity; the sand-grain relation is recalled from Blocken 2007; Hagbo used z0 = 3 m on terrain with 0.68 m cells, so published practice differs; the small-z0 range is the critic's recommendation

metrics.name: Fidelity and compute label
metrics.good: Each map carries its level (L1 screening, L2-lite comparative only, L2-full) with cell count and core-hours
metrics.bad: Unlabelled map, or L2-lite results presented as compliance evidence
metrics.method: Write the level, cell count and core-hours to MethodMetadata and show the label on every map
metrics.basis: Derived from one reported case (about 57 core-hours per million cells, linear scaling); L2-lite 2-5 M cells and L2-full tens of millions of cells are team assumptions

metrics.name: Decision-level validation against tunnel data
metrics.good: Class agreement with tunnel data at or above a team-set level (placeholder 80% of probes) and exceedance-probability bias within a team-set band (placeholder 5 percentage points), on AIJ cases
metrics.bad: Outside these bands, or no benchmark run; r and FAC2 alone presented as validation
metrics.method: Run the benchmark; compare comfort class and exceedance fraction at each probe against tunnel data; report with the VDI 3783-9 hit rate once opened
metrics.basis: Replaces FAC2 >= 0.5, |FB| <= 0.3, NMSE <= 4 from dispersion practice, which tolerate class-shifting speed errors; AIJ cases to run: the Niigata case E (Hagbo) plus a single tall building and a tall building among low-rise blocks (recalled, case identities to confirm); no supertall benchmark found

metrics.name: Descriptive statistics (FAC2, FB, NMSE)
metrics.good: Reported alongside, with no acceptance band adopted
metrics.bad: Used as pass/fail with bands taken from dispersion-model evaluation
metrics.method: Compute at benchmark probes
metrics.basis: Chang and Hanna 2004 bands were recalled differently in r1 and r2 (NMSE below 4 versus about 1.5) and not opened

metrics.name: Hit rate against reference data (COST 732 / VDI 3783-9 style)
metrics.good: 66% or higher (recalled, to confirm)
metrics.bad: Below 66%
metrics.method: Fraction of probes within stated tolerance of the reference
metrics.basis: Recalled from COST 732/VDI practice; Toronto only cites COST 732 as the guideline to follow; originals not opened

metrics.name: Agreement with wind-tunnel benchmark (Pearson r)
metrics.good: Report r per direction as supplementary information only
metrics.bad: Used as pass/fail: r is scale-invariant and would pass a model that underpredicts speeds by 35%
metrics.method: Correlation of CFD vs tunnel at probes for an AIJ benchmark
metrics.basis: Hagbo and Giljarhus Table 5: r 0.61 (247.5 deg) to 0.84 (180 deg), text says 0.71-0.84; mean speed differences -1% to -35%. The earlier 0.71-0.84 pass/fail band is corrected

metrics.name: Domain and blockage logged
metrics.good: Domain 6 Hmax high (5 above the tallest building), 15 Hmax downstream and blockage at most 3%, or the departure logged, in MethodMetadata
metrics.bad: Not logged
metrics.method: Compute from the case files
metrics.basis: Two peer-reviewed papers (S49, S06) quote the AIJ and COST 732 domain rules; the AIJ and COST 732 originals were not opened; whether the rules suffice for 305 m towers is unverified

metrics.name: Geometry detail near pedestrian zones
metrics.good: Features projecting more than 0.5 m modelled near pedestrian areas; under 1 m ignored elsewhere
metrics.bad: Entrance and corner detail removed
metrics.method: Check the mesh geometry against the Layer 0 detail list
metrics.basis: City of London requires features over 0.5 m near pedestrian areas; Toronto says dimensions under 1 m have no notable impact; the stricter rule applies near pedestrians

metrics.name: Solver version pinned
metrics.good: OpenFOAM Foundation v12 pinned for Eddy3D compatibility (it contains atmBoundaryLayer and nutkAtmRoughWallFunction), or v13 after re-test; version in MethodMetadata
metrics.bad: Unpinned or silently upgraded
metrics.method: Read the container tag
metrics.basis: Eddy3D uses OpenFOAM 12; the atmospheric boundary conditions were read in the OpenFOAM-12 source; Foundation v13 repository exists

metrics.name: Surrogate accuracy claim
metrics.good: Independently validated for supertall, dense downtown contexts
metrics.bad: Vendor claim only (for example 90%+ accuracy)
metrics.method: Run the surrogate and RANS on the same massing and compare
metrics.basis: Vendor statements; no independent validation opened

modules.method: Fidelity ladder. L0: M03 rules. L1: ML surrogate (Eddy3D Wind Predictor, GAN surrogate, Infrared.city API), screening only. L2-lite: OpenFOAM-12 steady RANS, comparative only: context to max(400 m, about 2H) plus approved towers; rotating cylindrical domain meshed once (6 Hmax high, 15 Hmax downstream, blockage at most 3%); inflow capped at gradient height with a consistent top condition; atmospheric rough wall upstream and small z0 on modelled ground; empty-domain homogeneity run; 1-2 m cells at probes (placeholder), about 2-5 M cells, 16 directions. L2-full: City of London mesh (0.3 m cells, 10 cells per canyon, prism layers), 16-36 directions, cluster or consultant. L3: consultant tunnel study (36 directions, about 50 probes). Validate on AIJ cases by class agreement and exceedance bias. M04 reads any VAFField, including imported CSV.
visualization: Contour map of VAF at 1.5 m per direction, diverging colour ramp centred on 1.0 (legend 0-2, editable), with streamlines
Vertical slice through the tower and podium at the worst corner
Residual and convergence plots for L2 runs, plus profile plots of U, k and epsilon (inlet versus building position) for the homogeneity run
Confusion matrix of comfort classes (CFD vs reference) with percent agreement, and a fidelity badge reading 'L1 screening only', 'L2-lite comparative only' or 'L2-full' with cell count and core-hours

modules.limits: CFD at massing stage cannot reliably predict gusts, flow separation or safety exceedances (Toronto). Steady RANS shows bias against tunnels. Surrogates have undisclosed training domains. L2-full is a cluster or consultant task and L2-lite is comparative only. No supertall benchmark was found: AIJ case E has a 60 m high-rise. Eddy3D needs Rhino 8, so a web tool imports its results or runs its own OpenFOAM service.
modules.human_judgment: Choosing the fidelity level, judging mesh quality and validation, deciding when a consultant wind-tunnel study is warranted, and signing off any safety conclusion.

modules.name: Outdoor thermal comfort and rain exposure
modules.effort: M: 6-8 person-days (UTCI engine, clamping and counters, time-base tag check, MRT input from the sun/shade module, driving-rain index, category maps)
modules.design_question: In which public spaces and seasons do wind, sun, temperature and rain give acceptable outdoor comfort, and where does tower-induced wind or canopy cover help or hurt?
inputs: WindClimate[time base] with concurrent temperature and humidity (concurrent-30y or TMYx); the choice is stored in MethodMetadata
ProbeWindSeries (mean speed series) from M04 on the same time base tag
Mean radiant temperature series from the sun/shadow module (other packet); fallback ladybug-comfort solar-adjusted MRT, labelled approximate
Hourly precipitation concurrent with wind direction (station record; availability in ECCC hourly files not verified)
CanopyCoverageTable from M03 and M07, zone tags and occupancy hours
outputs: UTCIMap: per probe and hour, UTCI and stress category with a validity flag (valid, clipped-calm, storm-excluded, out-of-range)
ThermalComfortSummary per zone and season, with excluded-hour counts
WindHelpsOrHurts flag per zone
RainExposureIndex per frontage and sector, and WeatherProtectionCoverage per frontage

parameters.name: Pedestrian-level mean wind speed
parameters.relationship: Higher wind lowers UTCI: relief in heat, added cold stress in cold. This tool feeds mean speed, not GEM (team choice). Calm (mean under 5 km/h most of the time) in full sun risks poor circulation, so Sitting-class wind is not automatically thermally good.

parameters.name: Mean radiant temperature (sun and shade)
parameters.relationship: Shade from tower, podium or trees lowers Tmrt -> lower UTCI in summer, but also removes winter solar gain. Tmrt minus air temperature must stay within -30 to +70 K for valid UTCI.

parameters.name: Air temperature and humidity
parameters.relationship: UTCI is the equivalent air temperature of a reference environment (50% RH with vapour pressure capped at 20 hPa, calm air, radiant temperature equal to air temperature); valid for air temperature -50 to 50 C and vapour pressure up to 5 kPa.

parameters.name: Wind reference conversion to 10 m
parameters.relationship: UTCI expects 10 m wind. Ladybug says 10 m speed is 1.5 times the speed at ground; a log law with z0 = 0.01 m (UTCI procedure, recalled) gives ln(10/0.01)/ln(h/0.01): 1.47 at 1.1 m, 1.38 at 1.5 m. Unscaled pedestrian speed -> cold stress understated.

parameters.name: Activity and clothing assumption
parameters.relationship: UTCI assumes walking at about 2.4 met with adaptive clothing; seated plaza users fall outside the assumption and the docs suggest PET for such cases, so sitting-zone results are less certain.

parameters.name: Time base and concurrency
parameters.relationship: A typical-year file is internally consistent but under-represents storms; a 30-year record keeps temperature, humidity and wind concurrent (Arctic outflow, 1-3 times per winter) but has no concurrent solar. M06 refuses inputs whose time-base tags differ.

parameters.name: Input clamping and exclusion
parameters.relationship: pythermalcomfort returns NaN below 0.5 or above 17 m/s (the official program accepts up to 30 m/s but documents 17). Clipping sheltered hours to 0.5 m/s and counting storm hours keeps calm zones in the denominator; dropping them biases shares.

parameters.name: Wind-driven rain exposure
parameters.relationship: Rain falling with wind from a sector slants onto frontages facing it; stronger wind and wider windward frontage -> more wetted pedestrian area. Magnitude not quantified; a driving-rain index (ISO 15927-3) is a candidate, not opened.

parameters.name: Weather-protection coverage
parameters.relationship: Continuous deep canopies and covered walkways shelter pedestrians from rain and, per Toronto and Hamilton, deflect downwash at the base. Coverage targets in Vancouver guidance were not opened.

metrics.name: UTCI category
metrics.good: 9 to 26 deg C: no thermal stress
metrics.bad: Above 32 (strong heat stress, up to extreme above 46) or below -13 (strong cold stress, down to extreme below -40)
metrics.method: Classify each hourly UTCI with thresholds 46/38/32/26(28)/9/0/-13/-27/-40; Ladybug splits 26-32 at 28 into slight and moderate heat stress
metrics.basis: Ladybug-comfort default thresholds implementing the Broede et al. scale; scale itself not opened

metrics.name: Input validity
metrics.good: 10 m wind 0.5-17 m/s; air temperature -50 to 50 C; Tr minus Ta -30 to 70 K; RH 0-100%; vapour pressure 0-5 kPa
metrics.bad: Outside range: result is NaN or unrealistic if extrapolated; UTCI can also be non-monotonic in wind speed
metrics.method: Enforce limit_inputs in pythermalcomfort
metrics.basis: pythermalcomfort documentation

metrics.name: Clamping rule and excluded hours
metrics.good: Calm hours clipped to 0.5 m/s; hours above 17 m/s or otherwise out of range counted per probe and shown as a separate class; shares use all occupied hours
metrics.bad: NaN hours silently dropped from the denominator
metrics.method: Counters per probe and season; show valid and excluded hours side by side
metrics.basis: Editable rule built on the documented validity limits; the 0.5 m/s clip is a team choice

metrics.name: Time base declared and matched
metrics.good: Concurrent temperature, humidity and wind from one record, or all variables from one TMYx year; the same tag on WindClimate, ProbeWindSeries and Tmrt; label shown on every map
metrics.bad: Typical-year temperature with a 30-year wind record, or any input with a different tag
metrics.method: Check the time-base tag of every input series; refuse to merge differing tags (schema check)
metrics.basis: Design rule; default is TMYx because solar is needed; M01 and M04 now emit a series per time base so the default has a consistent wind input

metrics.name: Share of occupied hours with no thermal stress
metrics.good: At least 50% of occupied hours in 9-26 C (editable placeholder)
metrics.bad: Below 25% of occupied hours (editable placeholder)
metrics.method: Count hours per zone in each UTCI category
metrics.basis: No sourced target; team to set per space type

metrics.name: Ground-to-10 m wind conversion
metrics.good: Factor computed from the declared probe height h as ln(10/z0)/ln(h/z0) with z0 = 0.01 m (about 1.38 at 1.5 m), sensitivity band shown
metrics.bad: Unscaled pedestrian speed fed into UTCI, or an undocumented factor
metrics.method: Compute the factor from the probe height; show a sensitivity band
metrics.basis: Ladybug states a 1.5 factor attributed to the Fiala model; the log-law form with z0 = 0.01 m and body height 1.1 m (factor 1.47) is recalled from the UTCI procedure, whose primary text was not opened

metrics.name: Weather-protection coverage
metrics.good: Higher share of retail and transit-plaza frontage under canopy than the baseline scheme
metrics.bad: Lower share than the baseline scheme
metrics.method: Canopy footprint along each frontage divided by frontage length
metrics.basis: No sourced target; City of Vancouver weather-protection guidance not opened

metrics.name: Driving-rain exposure
metrics.good: Smaller wetted frontage length than the baseline scheme
metrics.bad: Larger wetted frontage length than the baseline scheme
metrics.method: Weight hourly rain by wind direction and frontage orientation, reduced by canopy coverage
metrics.basis: Candidate method ISO 15927-3 not opened; no Vancouver threshold found

modules.method: Choose a time base: B) one TMYx year for all variables (default), or A) concurrent 30-year ECCC/ISD temperature, humidity and wind with Tmrt from the sun/shade module (cold-stress screening, no concurrent solar). Per probe and hour: air temperature and humidity from that base; mean pedestrian wind from M04 on the same base, converted to the UTCI 10 m convention with ln(10/z0)/ln(h/z0) (z0 default 0.01 m, h the probe height, editable), clipped to 0.5 m/s, excluded above 17 m/s and counted; Tmrt from the sun/shadow module. Compute UTCI with the Broede polynomial via pythermalcomfort with limits on; classify with the 10-threshold scale. Aggregate per zone and season over occupancy hours, excluded hours as their own class. Flag zones where wind moves the category versus a calm baseline. Rain: weight hourly precipitation by wind direction and frontage orientation and compare with canopy coverage.
visualization: Ground-plane false-colour map of percent of occupied hours in 'no thermal stress' (0-100%), seasonal toggle, with a grey excluded-hours overlay
Calendar heat map (day x hour) for a selected probe coloured by the UTCI scale (-40 to 46 C, diverging blue-white-red)
Stacked bars per zone of hours in each stress category plus a grey 'excluded' segment
Wind-effect arrow chips per zone (helps/hurts)
Plan of frontage lines coloured by driving-rain index (0-1), hatched where canopy coverage exists

libraries.role: Alternative implementation inside Grasshopper (needs Rhino 8)
libraries.license: Free for all users; source licence not stated

modules.limits: UTCI is an outdoor index; Tmrt needs a radiation model beyond Layer 0, and trees and surfaces ('City in Nature') are not modelled by default. The 10 m wind conversion rests on a recalled log-law form and UTCI can be non-monotonic in wind speed. A typical year under-represents Vancouver heat events and cold snaps; no future climate files. The rain method and weather-protection targets are unverified.
modules.human_judgment: Setting the acceptable stress level per space type, trading summer shade against winter sun, judging comfort for seated and children's uses outside the UTCI activity assumption, and deciding how much rain cover the public realm needs.
depends_on: EXT: Tmrt series from the sun/shadow module (other packet, id to be assigned; fallback ladybug-comfort MRT)

modules.name: Wind mitigation comparison and advisor
modules.effort: M: 5-7 person-days (scenario graph, delta maps, ordered mitigation library, significance scheme, vegetation rule)
modules.design_question: Which design changes reduce wind exceedances most, tried in order of large-scale massing first, then architectural details, then localised screens, and what does each cost the design?
inputs: ComfortMap scenarios: existing, proposed, mitigation, phasing
WindRiskField from M03
Geometry change log from Layer 0
Program and floor-area data
Vegetation objects (trees, planting) with declared leaf area density and foliage state, used only in mitigation scenarios
outputs: MitigationScenarioSet
DeltaComfortMap (scenario minus baseline) with City of London significance classes
RankedMitigations (3-tier order)
SignificantChangeLog: which edits require re-running M05
CanopyCoverageUpdate (to M06)

parameters.name: Orientation, siting and massing changes
parameters.relationship: Largest area of influence: building shape, height, podium and corner changes alter flow over the whole frontage; Toronto instructs applicants to try these first, before details or screens.

parameters.name: Canopies, recessed entrances, base articulation
parameters.relationship: Local mitigation at entrances and walkways; deep and wrap-around canopies redirect downwash away from ground and add rain cover (M06). Effect is confined to a small area and applied after massing options are exhausted.

parameters.name: Wind screens and landscaping
parameters.relationship: Screens at least 6 ft (about 1.8 m) tall and 20-40% porous diffused corner winds in one RWDI project; Toronto requires written City approval to rely on them, and landscaping must be effective at installation.

parameters.name: Vegetation in baseline versus mitigation scenarios
parameters.relationship: Toronto does not consider landscaping unless agreed with the City; City of London ignores landscape under 8 m in baselines. A 'City in Nature' scheme taking planting credit in massing runs would understate wind; trees enter only mitigation scenarios.

parameters.name: Construction phasing
parameters.relationship: Interim phases before later buildings arrive can be windier than the final scheme, so phased projects need separate scenarios.

parameters.name: Significant design changes
parameters.relationship: Changes in building count, orientation, setback, massing, height, tower offset from podium or canopies can alter wind enough to require a new study; any such edit marks results stale.

parameters.name: Significance of a class shift
parameters.relationship: City of London rates a change by class shift: windier by one class but still suitable is moderate adverse; safe becoming unsafe or suitable becoming unsuitable is major adverse. This replaces an undefined 'significant degradation'.

metrics.name: Net effect against existing conditions
metrics.good: Improves existing conditions where possible; no probe worsens by a class
metrics.bad: Major adverse: safe becomes unsafe or suitable becomes unsuitable (City of London); Hamilton: significant degradation, especially of safety
metrics.method: Delta ComfortMap per zone and season rated with the City of London scheme
metrics.basis: City of London 2019 significance tables; Hamilton assessment text

metrics.name: Mitigation order followed
metrics.good: Massing first, architectural details second, localised features third
metrics.bad: Screens or trees used to rescue an unmitigated massing
metrics.method: Check the mitigation scenario history
metrics.basis: Toronto 6.7.2 prioritisation

metrics.name: Vegetation excluded from baseline
metrics.good: No vegetation in Existing and Proposed baseline runs (landscape under 8 m ignored); trees only in mitigation scenarios, declared with leaf area density and foliage state and flagged as dependent on City approval
metrics.bad: Planting credited in massing or baseline runs
metrics.method: Check scenario objects against the vegetation rule
metrics.basis: Toronto: landscaping not considered unless agreed with the City; City of London: ignore landscape elements under 8 m in baseline studies; leaf area density values are unsourced

metrics.name: Significant-change trigger
metrics.good: No change in the Toronto 6.2 list since the last run
metrics.bad: Any listed change marks M04 results stale
metrics.method: Classify each Layer 0 edit against the list
metrics.basis: Toronto 6.2 significant design changes

metrics.name: Wind-screen specification
metrics.good: At least 1.8 m tall and 20-40% porous, confirmed by an M05 or tunnel re-run
metrics.bad: Lower or solid screens, or credit taken without a re-run
metrics.method: Check screen objects in the mitigation scenario and the re-run record
metrics.basis: One RWDI project recommendation (Cambridge MA 2021), not a standard; Toronto requires written City approval to rely on screens

modules.method: Maintain a scenario graph (Existing, Proposed, Mitigation A..n, Phase n). Baseline and massing scenarios exclude vegetation; trees enter only mitigation scenarios as porous media with declared leaf area density and foliage state, flagged approval-dependent. Each edit to Layer 0 is classified against the Toronto significant-change list and marks M04 results stale. For each scenario pair compute per-probe change in class and in exceedance fraction, rate it with the City of London significance scheme, and compute the area of public realm moved into or out of the required class. Rank candidate mitigations by tier (massing, architectural, localised) and by area improved, using results from re-runs rather than assumed effectiveness. The mitigation library stores sourced notes (screens at least 1.8 m tall and 20-40% porous, wrap-around corner canopies, podium step-backs) as hypotheses with their source project. Output the order, the deltas and a reason log for the board text.
visualization: Before/after slider on the ground-plane comfort map
Delta map: blue where class improves, red where it worsens, with safety-class changes outlined in black and significance class in the legend
Ordered list with a tier badge and area improved per option; vegetation options carry an 'approval needed' badge
Pareto scatter: public-realm area meeting target versus floor area or design intent lost

libraries.name: numpy / pandas
libraries.role: Scenario deltas and ranking (licences not re-verified)

libraries.name: plotly.js / three.js
libraries.role: Slider, delta overlay and Pareto chart

modules.limits: Mitigation effectiveness is project-specific. No general effectiveness coefficients were found, so each option needs a re-run in M05 or a tunnel test. Screens and trees are excluded at massing stage in Toronto-style reviews and need approval. The screen specification comes from one consultant report and is an editable assumption; no sourced leaf area density values exist.
modules.human_judgment: Which trade-off to accept (floor area, form, public programme, trees against wind), design intent and aesthetics, and whether to seek City approval for localised features.

modules.name: Elevated public terrace and sky-lobby wind check
modules.effort: M: about 5 person-days after M05 exists; wind-tunnel confirmation outside tool scope
modules.design_question: Are publicly accessible terraces, sky gardens and podium roofs high in the tower usable for their intended activity in each season, or do they need screens, enclosure or re-siting?
inputs: Layer 0 levels tagged public or amenity at height
VAFField with ReferenceSpec and inflow declaration to at least 1.2 H at terrace probes (CFD or ML roof-level prediction) from M05 or imported
WindClimate
CriteriaSet (with safety criterion)
Parapet or screen geometry
outputs: TerraceSuitabilityTable per level and season
RecommendedScreens or enclosure list

Hand-off notes: to P10 (tower height, corner treatment and taper used; no structural calculation here; confirm the current Vancouver Building By-law edition first), to SPAC/P10 (ice and snow shedding zones, unquantified) and to SYST (entrance and below-grade connection drafts, unquantified)

parameters.name: Height above ground
parameters.relationship: Wind speed increases with elevation, so terraces higher in the tower meet stronger wind; the brief's vertically distributed public uses raise exposure. A quantified gradient is not given in the opened sources.

parameters.name: Terrace position on the facade
parameters.relationship: Terrace corners and windward faces receive accelerated and downwashing flow; RWDI used guardrails at least 6 ft tall and wrap-around canopies to cut speeds at exposed terrace corners.

parameters.name: Season of use
parameters.relationship: Summer sitting use needs the calmest class; winter use is lower so Hamilton accepts some winter degradation, which can justify seasonal closure.

parameters.name: Parapet and screen height
parameters.relationship: Taller parapets or porous screens lower speed at terrace level; amount depends on geometry and is not quantified in sources.

parameters.name: Reference profile at terrace height
parameters.relationship: A VAF normalised near 10 m with a log-law inflow may not describe wind at 150-300 m; a wrong profile there scales terrace speeds and classes. Eddy3D ABL and OpenFOAM-12 atmBoundaryLayer use an uncapped log law; validity aloft is unverified.

metrics.name: Terrace comfort class
metrics.good: Sitting for seating terraces in the season of use (Toronto 10 km/h; City Lawson Occasional Sitting 4 m/s); Standing for circulation
metrics.bad: Walking or Uncomfortable (over 20 km/h at 20% in Toronto) for a space meant for sitting
metrics.method: Reuse the M04 engine with terrace probes
metrics.basis: Toronto Table 3 lists balconies and amenity terraces under Sitting; RWDI recommends sitting conditions for terraces and podiums; City of London lists balconies and terraces as Occasional Sitting

metrics.name: Terrace gust safety
metrics.good: Within the safety criterion of the chosen family (Toronto: gust at or below 90 km/h for 0.1% of hours or less; City Lawson: 15 m/s at 0.022%)
metrics.bad: Above the family's limit
metrics.method: 24 h annual exceedance at terrace probes
metrics.basis: Toronto Table 3; City of London safety table

metrics.name: Prediction confidence at height
metrics.good: Tunnel-validated
metrics.bad: Unvalidated RANS or surrogate at 100+ m levels
metrics.method: Read MethodMetadata from M05
metrics.basis: No sourced validation of height-level predictions in opened material

modules.method: Select Layer 0 spaces tagged public or amenity above grade. Place probes 1.5 m above the terrace floor on a grid and at corners (City of London lists upper-level terraces and balconies as critical locations). Obtain VAF with ReferenceSpec at those probes from M05 (CFD sampling, or the Eddy3D roof-level ML output when building geometry is supplied), refusing fields whose inflow profile is not declared to terrace height. Run the M04 engine with the terrace-specific required class, season of use and the family's safety criterion, and report class and safety. Where a terrace fails, propose screens (height and porosity from the M07 library), enclosure or relocation to a leeward face, and re-run. Add hand-off notes to P10, SPAC and SYST listing what changed.
visualization: Tower elevation or section with terrace markers coloured by summer and winter class
Per-level table with class, gust margin and confidence badge
Corner-hotspot plan for each terrace with screen suggestions
