modules.limits: Prediction at height is the least validated part of this packet; steady RANS and surrogates trained mainly on ground-level probes may not transfer to 150-300 m, and the inflow profile aloft is unverified. Wind tunnel testing is the reference. Structural and facade wind loads are separate (P10). Ice shedding and entrance drafts have no sourced criteria here. Safety sign-off at height needs a specialist.
modules.human_judgment: Programme decisions (open, seasonal closure, enclose or relocate), occupant safety sign-off, and how much high-level exposure is part of the design experience.

sources.title: Pedestrian Level Wind Study Terms of Reference Guide
sources.publisher: City of Toronto, Urban Design, with RWDI
sources.extract: Re-read in r1 and r2 (text extracted). Table 1 (Area 1 High over 100 m), Table 2, 3.b shifts; 5.1 scenarios incl. projects approved in last 5 years; 5.3 four seasons; 6.2 significant changes; 6.4.1 proximity radius about 350 m minimum plus tall buildings beyond; 6.4.2 CFD (COST 732, two-equation RANS or LES, 16 directions, safety may be assessed numerically or by experience); 6.4.4 30-year hourly data corrected for terrain and scaled to gradient height (600 m example) with established mathematical models, comfort 06:00-23:00 and safety 24 h; Table 3 three classes 10/15/20 km/h at 80% with zone mapping, 90 km/h gust at 0.1%; note 3 concerns wind speed (not GEM) under 5 km/h for the majority of the time (e.g. 80%); landscaping not considered unless agreed with the City; 6.7.2 mitigation order.

sources.title: Development Application Guidelines: Wind Study (last updated 20 February 2026)
sources.extract: Re-read in r1, rechecked in r2. Triggers (20 m, 44 m, 2x surroundings, 2+ buildings, 3 ha); qualitative CFD may simulate prevailing directions only; tunnel 36 directions, 400 m, sensors every 10 m and about 50 locations, sampling at least one hour of full-scale time; 30 years of hourly data; Table 1 under 10/14/17/20 km/h at 80%; Table 2 90 km/h gust at 0.1%; Summer May-Oct and Winter Nov-Apr although the text says 'four-season basis'; winter allowance. Adoption status unconfirmed: file name says 'ph1proposed'.

sources.title: Watermark Central, Cambridge MA: Pedestrian Wind Consultation (RWDI #1601643)
sources.extract: Re-read in r1. Four classes 6/8/10/12 mph GEM at 20% exceedance, 06:00-23:00; safety 56 mph at 0.1%; summer May-Oct, winter Nov-Apr; Boston Logan 1995-2015, anemometer 30 ft; 1200 ft radius, 86 sensors, 36 directions. Text: walking or strolling suit sidewalks, sitting for terraces and podiums, standing at main entrances. Vendor statement that criteria are widely accepted by municipalities.

sources.title: IDCP V3, Cambridge MA: Pedestrian Wind Study (RWDI #2101718)
sources.extract: Generalised flows (downwashing, corner acceleration, channelling); podium set-back, deep canopies, screens; screens at least 6 ft tall and 20-40% porous; guardrails and wrap-around canopies at terrace corners; effect best confirmed by tunnel tests.

sources.title: Wind Study Terms of Reference 2026
sources.extract: Study may be required for buildings of 6 storeys or more; preliminary study with at least 15 sensors; final tunnel study with 1:500 model and 480 m context; comfort judged on wind force, thermal comfort and wind chill.

sources.title: Pedestrian Wind Comfort Assessment Using CFD Simulations With Varying Number of Wind Directions
sources.extract: Re-read in r1 and r2. OpenFOAM steady RANS (realizable k-epsilon) on AIJ case E (Niigata building complex, 60 m high-rise); U_ref at 10 m = 5 m/s, results at 2 m; cylindrical domain with height 6 H_max (guidelines: 5 H above the tallest), outlet and lateral 15 H_max, slip top; terrain rough wall z0 = 3.00 m with wall functions on 0.68 m cells, buildings smooth on 0.34 m cells; y+ about 9x10^3 on terrain and 7x10^3 on buildings in the text (Table 1 lists about 7x10^2 for buildings); 'a version of' Lawson, mean speed only, 4/6/8/10 m/s at 5%, no distress criterion; class agreement by area against 64 directions 79/92/96/99% (4/8/16/32; Table 7 78.66/91.61/95.84/99.01), authors call 8 directions insufficient; Table 5 r 0.61-0.84 (text says 0.71-0.84); mean-speed difference -1% to -35%; no FAC2, hit rate or NMSE. Reference list cites Franke 2007 (COST 732), Tominaga 2008 (AIJ), City of London 2019.

sources.title: Numerical Study of Flow Structure and Pedestrian Level Wind Comfort Inside Urban Street Canyons (arXiv 1703.08963)
sources.publisher: Pancholy et al., University of Canterbury (preprint)
sources.extract: Idealised steady-RANS canyons; wind comfort via Extended Land Beaufort Scale; gap of 1x height comfortable, 2x height gave a larger uncomfortable zone on the upwind face of the downwind building; building width had little effect.

sources.title: Deriving the operational procedure for the Universal Thermal Climate Index (UTCI), Brode et al.
sources.extract: Abstract re-read in r2 (PubMed record, DOI 10.1007/s00484-011-0454-1). UTCI is the air temperature of a reference environment (50% RH with vapour pressure capped at 20 hPa, calm air, radiant temperature equal to air temperature) giving the same dynamic physiological response (UTCI-Fiala model with adaptive clothing); fast polynomial routines and a stress scale are provided. The abstract does not mention the 10 m wind height or conversion to body height; full text not opened.

sources.title: ladybug_comfort.parameter.utci documentation
sources.extract: Default UTCI thresholds in deg C: -40, -27, -13, 0, 9 (cold), 26, 28, 32, 38, 46 (heat); Ladybug splits 26-32 into slight and moderate heat stress at 28.

sources.title: ladybug_comfort.utci documentation

Wind input is speed 10 m above ground; states 10 m speed is 1.5 times the speed felt at ground in the original Fiala model (no specific citation); UTCI is outdoor only, assumes walking at about 2.4 met; PET recommended otherwise. sources.title: Climate of Vancouver
sources.extract: Winter Arctic outflow 1-3 times per winter; Dec 2006 windstorm gusts 70-125 km/h; summer sea breezes; airport record high 34.4 C (2009). No seasonal wind-rose data.

sources.title: Climate.OneBuilding.Org
sources.extract: EPW/TMYx files built from NOAA ISD hourly data through 2023 using TMY/ISO 15927-4; disclaimer only, no licence; says nothing on wind data quality.

sources.title: AIJ guidelines for practical applications of CFD to pedestrian wind environment around buildings (Tominaga et al.)
sources.extract: Not opened (doi.org redirects to Elsevier; ScienceDirect returned HTTP 403 in r2). Its domain recommendation (6 Hmax high, 20 Hmax long, blockage at most 3%) was read second-hand in Kastner and Dogan 2018 (S49) and Hagbo and Giljarhus (S06). AIJ benchmark case identities beyond case E are not confirmed.

sources.title: Higher Buildings Policy Review (full review document)
sources.extract: Named in the brief; HTTP 403 (also for syc.vancouver.ca exhibit summary and Bay Parkade FAQ files in r2). Search snippet: review covers design, public benefits, sustainability and climate considerations (wind and shadows). Unverified.

sources.title: Wind Microclimate Guidelines for Developments in the City of London (August 2019)
sources.extract: Opened in r1, re-read in r2 (text extracted). Approach table by building height (above 100 m: tunnel or CFD for massing, then tunnel and CFD by independent consultants); 36 directions; models within 400 m plus taller buildings beyond; consented or future buildings immediately around the site at any height and those taller than the surrounding average within 300 m, demolished-site case if existing building over 40 m; features over 0.5 m near pedestrians modelled, landscape under 8 m ignored in baselines; Harris-Deaves/ESDU 01008 profile; reference height ideally above 100 m, probabilities scaled to 120 m, scale factors 0.96 (100 m) to 1.48 (600 m); tunnel mean typically 10-15 min; probes at 1.5 m; CFD mesh 0.3 m near critical points, 10 cells across canyon, 3 prism layers below 1.5 m, avoid standard k-epsilon (realisable k-epsilon robust, k-omega SST allowed on a suitable mesh). City Lawson criteria on mean and GEM at 5%: 2.5/4/6/8 m/s with no stated hours window; safety 15 m/s at 0.022%; worst season plus June-August; significance tables; cyclist section (15 m/s applies to cyclists, a probe at least every 40 m on cycling paths); Annex A Weibull fits from Heathrow 1973-2017 and City Airport 1988-2017, corrected with ESDU 01008 and not valid for other areas.

sources.title: Glossary, Canadian Climate Data (ECCC)
sources.extract: Re-read in r2. Wind speed usually observed at 10 m as an average over a one-, two- or ten-minute period ending at the observation time; direction a two-minute average in tens of degrees, true (not magnetic), 36 = north, a value of zero denotes calm; gust is an instantaneous peak; the glossary does not say which period applies to hourly data (see S53).

sources.title: Search Historical Climate Data: stations (ECCC), query 'Vancouver Harbour'
sources.extract: Two stations match: VANCOUVER HARBOUR (hourly and daily, year options 2023-2026) and VANCOUVER HARBOUR CS (hourly, daily, monthly, year options 1976-2026). The page does not state hourly coverage, wind sensor presence or exposure; station and climate IDs not shown.

sources.title: Eddy3D docs: Atmospheric Boundary Layer (ABL)
sources.extract: Re-read in r2. Log-law inflow; reference height Zref default 10 m, reference velocity default 5 m/s per direction, roughness length z0 default 1 m (Revised Davenport terrain classes 0.0002-2 m), ground/displacement height Zgnd; terrain type describes what the wind crosses upwind of the site, not the site itself; one solver case per direction. The page is silent on wall functions, ground roughness treatment, horizontal homogeneity, gradient height and the top boundary.

sources.title: OpenFOAM-13 repository
sources.extract: Public repository 'OpenFOAM Foundation repository for OpenFOAM version 13'; README states GNU GPL version 3; no releases or tags shown, so v12 is no longer the newest Foundation version.

sources.title: Higher Buildings Policy (PDF 0.9 MB) as linked on Shape Your City Key Documents
sources.extract: Linked from the project page under Key Documents; the page shows only a 'file will begin downloading' interstitial; its /download link redirects to guidelines.vancouver.ca, which returned HTTP 403 in r2. No policy text was read. A manual download by a team member could settle the microclimate wording.

sources.title: Streamlining meshing methodologies for annual urban CFD simulations (Kastner and Dogan, eSim 2018)
sources.extract: Opened in r2 (text extracted). Reports the AIJ box domain as 6 Hmax high, 20 Hmax long and blockage at most 3% (15 Hmax downstream in its figure); proposes a cylindrical domain meshed once for many wind directions (up to 72 or more); OpenFOAM 4.1, k-omega SST, atmospheric inlet profile from friction velocity and z0; ground and buildings share wall-function conditions; lab-scale validation (Jiang et al. 2003) with z0 = 0.005 m; coarse mesh 263,919 cells took 15 h 10 min 47 s on one core of a 2018 Threadripper 1950X (box domain); cylindrical domain 21% more cells.

sources.title: OpenFOAM-12 atmBoundaryLayer class description
sources.extract: Opened in r2. Velocity U = (u*/kappa) ln((z - zg + z0)/z0) with u* from Uref at Zref; k = u*^2/sqrt(Cmu); epsilon = u*^3/(kappa (z - zg + z0)); parameters flowDir, zDir, Uref, Zref, z0, zGround, kappa 0.41, Cmu 0.09. No cap at Zref or at a gradient height: the log law applies at all heights.

sources.title: OpenFOAM-12 nutkAtmRoughWallFunction class description
sources.extract: Opened in r2. Provides turbulent kinematic viscosity for atmospheric velocity profiles and is designed to be used with atmBoundaryLayerInletVelocity; takes a surface roughness length z0 (usage: type nutkAtmRoughWallFunction; z0 uniform ...). The description does not state how z0 enters or whether homogeneity is guaranteed.

sources.title: CFD simulation of the atmospheric boundary layer: wall function problems (Blocken, Stathopoulos, Carmeliet)
sources.extract: Not opened: the DOI resolves (Elsevier PII S135223100600834X) but ScienceDirect returned HTTP 403. The relation between sand-grain roughness and z0 (about 9.793 z0/Cs) and the horizontal-inhomogeneity problem are recalled from the r2 critique, not read.

sources.title: Technical Documentation, Digital Archive of Canadian Climatological Data (ECCC)
sources.extract: Opened in r2 (text extracted, modified 2023-01-16). Hourly wind speed is usually observed at 10 m; for aviation stations it is the average over the two-minute period ending at observation time (one-minute mean until the late 1980s); the only historical 10-minute means come from synoptic reports made four times a day. Direction codes: 36 = north, 00 = calm. Wind character and gust speed at 10 m are reported since 1994 (archived January 2006).

flags.claim: The City of Vancouver publishes numeric pedestrian wind-comfort criteria or a mandatory wind-study trigger.
flags.detail: None found. vancouver.ca, guidelines.vancouver.ca, bylaws.vancouver.ca, council.vancouver.ca and rezoning.vancouver.ca returned HTTP 403 again in r1; the Shape Your City copy of the Higher Buildings Policy returned only a download interstitial. Snippets show only a qualitative Higher Buildings Policy microclimate criterion and an example rezoning condition. Ask the Rezoning Centre.

flags.claim: Higher Buildings Policy wording: a higher building should not contribute to adverse microclimate effects.
flags.detail: Taken from search snippets of the 2011 and 2018 versions. The 1997 PDF named in the brief and the current 2026 review documents could not be opened. The 1997 policy as amended governs until Council adopts the updated policy (targeted spring 2027); the amendment trail itself is unverified.

flags.claim: Default criteria for Vancouver runs are the Toronto 2022 three-class set (Sitting 10, Standing 15, Walking 20 km/h GEM at 80%; safety gust 90 km/h at 0.1% annual).
flags.detail: Updated in r1 (earlier text merged 'RWDI/Toronto'). Chosen as a Canadian downtown tall-building analog because no Vancouver set was found; Hamilton 2026 (10/14/17/20 km/h, equal or stricter at shared classes), RWDI mph and City Lawson are selectable, each with its own safety criterion. Edits stay visible as team assumptions.

flags.claim: Toronto, Hamilton and City of London trigger rules are used as stand-ins for 'when Vancouver requires a wind study'.
flags.detail: All three place a 244-305 m tower in the highest tier (wind-tunnel evidence). Vancouver practice is unconfirmed; for an ideas competition a CFD-level screening is assumed adequate.

flags.claim: Lawson thresholds and RWDI/Toronto thresholds are interchangeable.
flags.correction: They differ in exceedance basis and speed limits: Lawson-type sets use m/s at 5% of time (City Lawson 2.5/4/6/8 m/s on mean and GEM); RWDI/Toronto/Hamilton use GEM in km/h or mph at 20%. Using one speed table with the other exceedance gives wrong classes.
flags.detail: M04 enforces one family per run and shows the basis next to each result.

flags.claim: Airport (YVR) or typical-year EPW wind equals the wind at the downtown site.
flags.correction: Toronto requires 30 years of hourly airport data corrected for terrain and scaled via gradient height to the site; a typical-meteorological-year file is not a 30-year record and under-represents storms.
flags.detail: M01 shows a data-quality badge and logs the correction model.

flags.claim: Early CFD can certify gust-safety compliance of a supertall scheme.
flags.correction: Toronto states CFD struggles with separation, eddies and gusts and is not suited to safety-based issues; wind-tunnel testing is required for high triggers. Steady RANS also showed bias against tunnels.
flags.detail: M05 labels outputs by fidelity level and M04 shows safety results as indicative below L3.

flags.claim: Calmer is always better: a Sitting-class wind condition is automatically good for outdoor use.
flags.correction: Toronto notes GEM under 5 km/h most of the time can cause low air circulation, exhaust build-up and heat in full sun.
flags.detail: M04 raises a low-wind flag and M06 tests the thermal side. (r2 note: the Toronto note refers to wind speed, not GEM; see the r2 flag below.)

flags.claim: Narrow tower gaps are always windier (simple Venturi rule).
flags.detail: Toronto, Hamilton and RWDI describe channelling in narrow gaps, but an idealised steady-RANS study found larger uncomfortable zones at gap = 2x height than at 1x height. The relationship is non-monotonic and unquantified for supertall towers. r2: M03 now distinguishes through-passages from closed gaps.

flags.claim: Infrared.city and other ML surrogates reach 90%+ accuracy within a minute.
flags.detail: Vendor claim; no method or independent validation opened. Training domain unknown; transfer to 244-305 m towers in dense downtown is unproven.

flags.claim: Eddy3D can be embedded in the open-source web tool.
flags.detail: Docs say it is free for all users but state no source licence, and it needs Rhino 8 on Windows or macOS. Treat it as an external tool whose CSV output is imported, until its licence is confirmed. Its GPL-3.0 OpenFOAM solvers are separate.

flags.claim: A hit rate of 66% or more validates a CFD run (COST 732/VDI practice).
flags.detail: Recalled from memory; Toronto only cites COST 732 as the guideline. Original not opened in r1 or r2. M05 lists hit rate beside decision-level metrics and does not use it alone.

flags.claim: UTCI wind input equals about 1.5 times the wind felt at ground.
flags.detail: Ladybug documentation attributes the factor to the original Fiala model without citation; pythermalcomfort gives no conversion; the UTCI primary documentation was not opened. Kept as an editable default with a sensitivity band; r2 replaces the fixed 1.5 with a probe-height formula (see r2 flag).

flags.claim: Target of at least 50% of occupied hours in the UTCI 'no thermal stress' band; rule weights and cut-offs in the M03 risk index.
flags.detail: No sourced targets. These are editable placeholders and must be recalibrated against M05 runs and project goals.

flags.claim: Claude Code skills or MCP servers exist for CFD, OpenFOAM or urban wind analysis.
flags.detail: The MCP registry and skill catalogue searches returned nothing in round 1, in r1 and again in r2. A custom MCP wrapper would have to be built.

flags.claim: RWDI and Toronto share one GEM criteria set of 10/15/20 km/h at 80%.
flags.correction: Treat Toronto 2022 (three classes 10/15/20 km/h), Hamilton 2026 (four classes 10/14/17/20 km/h) and RWDI (four classes 6/8/10/12 mph, about 9.7/12.9/16.1/19.3 km/h) as separate CriteriaSets, each with its own safety criterion.
flags.detail: Toronto Table 3 has no Strolling class; RWDI and Hamilton do, and Hamilton's 14 and 17 km/h differ from RWDI's 8 and 10 mph. Evidence: RWDI Cambridge report (S03), Toronto Table 3 (S01), Hamilton Table 1 (S02), re-read in r1.

flags.claim: Toronto and Hamilton both require at least 16 CFD wind directions.
flags.correction: The 16-direction CFD minimum is a Toronto 6.4.2 requirement. Hamilton's qualitative CFD may simulate only the prevailing directions (assessment still weights all directions) and Hamilton requires 36 directions only for tunnel tests; City of London asks for 36 in all studies.
flags.detail: Hamilton Technical Requirements 1.A and 1.B (S02), Toronto 6.4.2 (S01), City of London general requirements (S43).

flags.claim: Steady RANS in Hagbo and Giljarhus achieved Pearson r of 0.71-0.84, so 0.71 is the lower end and r can serve as pass/fail.
flags.correction: Table 5 lists r down to 0.61 (247.5 degrees) up to 0.84 (180 degrees); the 0.71-0.84 range comes from the text only. r is scale-invariant and cannot detect the -1% to -35% mean-speed bias the same paper reports, so it is supplementary only.
flags.detail: Frontiers 2022, Table 5 and validation text, re-read in r1 (S06). M05 now uses decision-level metrics (r2).

flags.claim: Butterfly is a viable Python API for an OpenFOAM (Foundation v12) pipeline.
flags.correction: Butterfly is unmaintained: latest commits 11 Sep 2020; the only OpenFOAM compatibility commit seen targets ESI OF1706+. Build case templates directly for the pinned Foundation version or use Eddy3D-generated cases.
flags.detail: GitHub commit history opened in r1 (S16). Foundation v13 also exists (S47), so v12 is pinned deliberately for Eddy3D compatibility.

flags.claim: The Lawson criteria in Hagbo and Giljarhus are a verified mean/GEM criteria set.
flags.correction: The paper uses 'a version of' Lawson, mean speed only, with no distress or safety criterion. The verified primary Lawson-type set in this packet is the City of London 2019 City Lawson (mean and GEM, 2.5/4/6/8 m/s at 5%, safety 15 m/s at 0.022%).
flags.detail: Hagbo and Giljarhus Table 4 and discussion (S06); City of London 2019 (S43). The Hagbo set is kept as comfort-only and unverified lineage; safety output is blocked for it.

flags.claim: RWDI considers sidewalks to need strolling or better.
flags.correction: RWDI says conditions comfortable for walking or strolling are appropriate for sidewalks. Sidewalk requirement: Walking, with Strolling as a preference where the set has that class.
flags.detail: RWDI Cambridge report, section 5.1 (S03); Toronto Table 3 also maps sidewalks to Walking (S01).

flags.claim: A modelled context radius of about 350 m is adequate for this tower.
flags.correction: Toronto states 350 m is a minimum and that tall buildings outside it that could influence the site must be included; Hamilton and City of London use 400 m. For H = 244-305 m, 350-400 m is about 1.1-1.6 H and the brief names approved towers of similar height. Use at least max(400 m, about 2H) plus influential towers beyond.
flags.detail: Toronto 6.4.1 (S01), Hamilton 1 (S02), City of London CFD requirements (S43). The 2H term is a team assumption.

flags.claim: Minimum context radius max(400 m, about 2H), with approved and future towers as a mandatory cumulative scenario.
flags.detail: The 350 m and 400 m minima are sourced; the 2H term and the mandatory cumulative case are editable team choices justified by the VTC context. COST 732 and AIJ domain rules were not opened to confirm.

flags.claim: Imported VAF data (Eddy3D, tunnel, consultant CSV) share one normalisation reference.
flags.detail: They do not necessarily. The Eddy3D VAF page names no reference height; its ABL component defaults to Zref 10 m, 5 m/s and z0 1 m; City of London uses a reference above 100 m; Hagbo normalise at 10 m. M04 therefore requires a ReferenceSpec on every VAFField and refuses to classify on a mismatch.

flags.claim: ECCC hourly station speeds can be treated as hourly mean winds, and Vancouver Harbour CS provides a usable downtown cross-check.
flags.detail: ECCC states speeds are 1-, 2- or 10-minute means ending at the observation; no sourced conversion factor was found. Vancouver Harbour CS appears in the ECCC station list (hourly year options 1976-2026) but wind sensor presence, hourly coverage and exposure were not verified. (r2: the averaging part is resolved, see the r2 FALSE_ASSUMPTION flag; the Harbour CS part remains unverified.)

flags.claim: Winter and spring storm winds set the worst comfort class in Vancouver.
flags.detail: The statement came from Ontario practice. Vancouver's strong winds are described as Pacific storms and winter outflow, but no seasonal wind-rose source was opened. M04 derives the governing season from the M01 wind rose instead.

flags.claim: M04 stays core as an importer and classifier; core users get M01-M03 plus M04 only when a VAF file is imported.
flags.detail: Resolves the core-versus-v1 conflict with M05 (hosted OpenFOAM is not feasible before 30 Nov). The UI states that without a VAFField only M03 screening is shown. An Eddy3D workflow guide and import template are the minimal VAF path.

flags.claim: UTCI runs by default on a TMYx time base; calm hours are clipped to 0.5 m/s and hours above 17 m/s are excluded and counted.
flags.detail: TMYx keeps temperature, humidity, solar and wind internally consistent. The 30-year concurrent option has no concurrent solar and is used for cold-stress screening. The clipping rule is a team choice built on the pythermalcomfort limits (S12); excluded hours stay in the denominator.

flags.claim: Weather-protection coverage and wind-driven rain exposure can be judged against Vancouver guidance.
flags.detail: City of Vancouver weather-protection guidance and any rain thresholds could not be opened; ISO 15927-3 driving-rain index not opened. M06 reports relative comparison against the baseline scheme only.

flags.claim: CFD acceptance bands FAC2 at least 0.5, absolute FB at most 0.3, NMSE at most 4.
flags.detail: Recalled from air-quality-model evaluation practice (Chang and Hanna 2004), not opened and not a wind-comfort standard. Editable placeholders until COST 732, VDI 3783-9 or AIJ texts are read. (r2: withdrawn as acceptance bands, see the r2 FALSE_ASSUMPTION flag.)

flags.claim: The Hamilton guideline is an adopted City document.
flags.detail: Text says 'last updated February 20, 2026' but the file name ends 'ph1proposed'; the text also says 'four-season basis' while listing two seasons. Adoption status and the season definition should be confirmed with Hamilton staff.

flags.claim: ECCC 1-, 2- or 10-minute mean speeds read higher than hourly means, so unconverted data inflate exceedances; a conversion factor should be applied to reach hourly means.
flags.correction: Treat sampled ECCC means as hourly-mean estimates with no multiplicative conversion. Log the sampling period as metadata, and derive pedestrian gusts from VAF and turbulence only.
flags.detail: A single short-period mean sampled at the observation time has the same expected value as the hourly mean and only more scatter; Durst/ESDU gust-factor curves relate the maximum short-duration mean within an hour to the hourly mean, so they do not apply to one sample. A factor of about 1.05-1.15 would lower every speed; for a Weibull shape near 2, a 10% cut turns a 20% exceedance into about 14% (checked arithmetic: exp(-ln5/0.81)), enough to shift a class. Evidence: ECCC glossary (S44) and technical documentation (S53): aviation-station hourly speed is a 2-minute mean ending at the observation (1-minute until the late 1980s); Toronto and Hamilton ask for hourly data with no conversion (S01, S02); City of London tunnel means are typically 10-15 min (S43). Supersedes the r1 UNVERIFIED flag on ECCC averaging.

flags.claim: CFD acceptance bands FAC2 >= 0.5, |FB| <= 0.3, NMSE <= 4 (Chang and Hanna 2004) are suitable placeholders for pedestrian wind-speed validation.
flags.correction: Use decision-level validation: comfort-class agreement and exceedance-probability bias against tunnel data on AIJ benchmark cases, plus the VDI 3783-9 hit rate once opened. Keep FAC2, FB and NMSE descriptive only and adopt no NMSE band.
flags.detail: The bands come from dispersion-model evaluation (concentrations spanning orders of magnitude). For speeds they allow factor-of-2 and 30% bias errors, each enough to shift comfort classes; S06 itself reports -1% to -35% mean-speed differences that a |FB| <= 0.3 band would partly accept. Round 1 recalled NMSE below 4; the r2 critic recalls below about 1.5; neither source text was opened, so the NMSE value is withdrawn. AIJ case E (S06) is a 60 m high-rise complex, not a supertall tower. Supersedes the r1 UNVERIFIED flag on these bands.

flags.claim: City Lawson comfort is assessed 'for 95% of comfort hours' (the 06:00-23:00 convention).
flags.correction: Run the City Lawson CriteriaSet on 24 h data for comfort and safety, using the Vancouver climate, with only the thresholds transferred, not the London climate coefficients.
flags.detail: The City of London 2019 guideline states no hours restriction in its comfort criteria or results sections; Annex A builds seasonal and annual Weibull fits from Heathrow (1973-2017) and City Airport (1988-2017) records and says the coefficients are not valid for other areas (S43, re-read in r2). The 06:00-23:00 window is Toronto, Hamilton and RWDI practice (S01-S03).

flags.claim: A probe in an empty domain should reproduce the undisturbed profile speed at 1.5 m within 5% when the ABL uses Eddy3D defaults (Zref 10 m, z0 1 m).
flags.correction: Test horizontal homogeneity of U, k and epsilon at 1.5 m, 10 m, H/2 and H at the building position. Use an atmospheric rough wall function with the inlet z0 on the approach fetch and a small z0 on the explicitly modelled ground; take the reference speed above 100 m.
flags.detail: With z0 = 1 m, 1.5 m lies in the roughness sublayer where the log law is not physical, and a standard rough wall function needs a sand-grain height near 20 m (about 9.793 z0/Cs, Blocken et al. 2007, recalled, not opened), incompatible with City of London near-ground meshing (0.3 m cells, 3 prism layers below 1.5 m, S43). Eddy3D ABL docs (S46, re-read in r2) give defaults Zref 10 m, z0 1 m and are silent on wall functions and the top boundary; OpenFOAM-12 provides nutkAtmRoughWallFunction for this purpose (S51). The test either fails or passes for the wrong reason.

flags.claim: Toronto's low-wind note concerns GEM under 5 km/h.
flags.correction: The note concerns wind speed (mean) under 5 km/h for the majority of the time (e.g. 80%); M04 bases the flag on mean speed and quotes 80% as an example.
flags.detail: Toronto Table 3 note 3 (S01, re-read in r2): 'wind speeds lower than 5 km/h for majority of the time (e.g., 80%)'. The r1 flag on 'calmer is always better' carried the GEM wording.

flags.claim: Station wind is transferred to the site per 22.5 degree sector with a named model, and the default reference height is 120 m.
flags.detail: Replaces a single site roughness. The downtown site sits on a peninsula, so some sectors cross water (Burrard Inlet, English Bay, False Creek) and others dense city; Eddy3D defines roughness as the terrain the wind crosses upwind (S46). The transfer model is Deaves-Harris/ESDU 01008 as City of London names it, or a log law capped at gradient height (Toronto example 600 m); 120 m is London's convention (S43) applied to Vancouver. Vancouver per-sector z0 values are not sourced; ESDU 01008 was not opened.

flags.claim: Which criteria family, station, seasons and hours City of Vancouver staff accept for downtown tower rezonings.
flags.detail: The attempt in r1 and r2 to obtain recent downtown rezoning wind reports failed: rezoning.vancouver.ca, vancouver.ca, guidelines.vancouver.ca, syc.vancouver.ca and council domains returned HTTP 403; Shape Your City documents redirect to those hosts; the Bay Parkade FAQ names no wind study. The Toronto default therefore stays a team assumption. Action: a team member downloads two or three reports by hand and fills the M02 PrecedentTable.

flags.claim: A standard rough wall function with z0 = 1 m needs a sand-grain height ks of about 9.793 z0/Cs, about 20 m.
flags.detail: Relation recalled from Blocken, Stathopoulos and Carmeliet 2007 (S52); the DOI resolves but the paper could not be opened. Hagbo and Giljarhus ran z0 = 3 m on terrain with 0.68 m cells (S06), so published practice differs from the recommended set-up. M05 marks the wall-function metric unverified.

flags.claim: Isotropic gust estimates from TKE (sqrt(2k/3)) understate streamwise turbulence by about 20-40%.
flags.detail: OpenFOAM-12 atmBoundaryLayer sets k = u*^2/sqrt(Cmu), about 3.3 u*^2, which gives sqrt(2k/3) of about 1.5 u* (S50, arithmetic checked); surface-layer sigma_u of about 2.4-2.5 u* is recalled, not opened. GEM exceeds the mean only where turbulence intensity exceeds about 28% (1 + 3I > 1.85, by definition in S01), so missing turbulence data makes GEM collapse to the mean. M04 declares g and an anisotropy factor and flags RANS-based GEM as indicative.

flags.claim: L2-lite (2-5 M cells, 16 directions, comparative only) and the compute estimates for each fidelity level.
flags.detail: Derived from one reported run: 263,919 cells took 15 h 10 min on one 2018 core (S49), about 57 core-hours per million cells, scaled linearly. 2-5 M cells x 16 directions is roughly 1,800-4,600 core-hours; tens of millions of cells at City of London mesh rules would be about 18,000-46,000 core-hours (20-50 M cells, an assumption). Iteration counts rise with mesh size, so these are lower bounds; no measured supertall run exists. L2-full is a cluster or consultant task; the 1-2 m cell size is a placeholder.

flags.claim: Inflow profile capped at gradient height, a consistent top boundary condition, and a declaration up to at least 1.2 H on every VAFField.
flags.detail: OpenFOAM-12 atmBoundaryLayer is an uncapped log law (S50) and the AIJ-style domain for H = 305 m is about 1.8 km high (S49), well above the Toronto 600 m gradient-height example (S01); Hagbo used a slip top (S06). The cap, the Richards-Hoxey top condition (recalled) and the 1.2 H declaration are team choices to be validated.

flags.claim: UTCI wind conversion: ln(10/z0)/ln(h/z0) with z0 = 0.01 m, giving 1.47 at 1.1 m and 1.38 at 1.5 m.
flags.detail: The log-law form and z0 = 0.01 m are recalled from the UTCI operational procedure; the PubMed abstract (S08) and the UTCI web page do not state them and the full text was not opened. The arithmetic is checked and the 1.47 value agrees with Ladybug's 1.5 (S11). Applicability of a log law inside a built canopy is unknown.

flags.claim: Passage and podium literature (Blocken et al. on passages; Tsang, Kwok and Hitchcock 2012 on podium, separation and dimensions) supports downgrading the 'narrow gaps accelerate' rule.
flags.detail: Both are recalled from the r2 critique and not opened (journal and page details to confirm). The downgrade rests on the opened idealised study (S07), which found a non-monotonic gap effect. M03 now separates through-passages from closed gaps and keeps the rule an editable placeholder.

flags.claim: The M03 composite 0-100 risk index stays hidden until a CalibrationLog of at least about 10 massings with L2 runs exists.
flags.detail: No sourced scoring scheme or calibration set exists; a composite number on a board would give false precision to a jury-facing output. The count of 10 is a team placeholder. Per-rule flags are shown instead.

flags.claim: AIJ benchmark cases for a single tall building and a tall building among low-rise blocks are suitable validation targets.
flags.detail: Recalled from the r2 critique; only case E (Niigata complex, 60 m high-rise) was confirmed, via S06. Tominaga et al. 2008 (S40) was not opened; case identities and data access must be checked. No benchmark at 244-305 m was found.

flags.claim: A stability proxy (hour of day, cloud, temperature) tags Arctic-outflow, clear-night and sea-breeze hours.
flags.detail: Neutral transfer and neutral CFD misrepresent stable and thermally driven hours, which are the cold-and-windy events M06 cares about (Arctic outflow 1-3 times per winter, S37). The proxy thresholds are user-editable and unsourced; the share of tagged hours is reported beside the neutral statistics.

flags.claim: Ice and snow shedding from a 244-305 m tower, and wind- and stack-driven drafts at tower entrances and the below-grade transit connection.
flags.detail: The r2 critique lists both as missing. No sourced relationship or criterion was found, so no metric is given. M08 emits hand-off notes to P10/SPAC (ice and snow) and SYST (drafts); M04 does not assess them.

unresolved_relationships: Quantified reduction of pedestrian-level GEM per metre of tower-to-podium step-back, podium height or canopy depth (direction sourced, magnitude not); Tsang, Kwok and Hitchcock 2012 on podium, separation and tall-building dimensions is recalled and not opened.

Gap-to-height ratio that minimises channelling between adjacent supertall towers (Venturi versus buffeting); only idealised low-rise RANS results seen (S07); passage studies reporting wind-blocking (Blocken and co-authors) not opened.

Dominant strong-wind directions and speeds at the downtown Vancouver site compared with Vancouver International Airport and ECCC Vancouver Harbour CS, including Burrard Inlet channelling and winter outflow; needs ECCC or site data.
Percentage speed reduction from chamfered, rounded, stepped or re-entrant corners on a 244-305 m tower.

General effectiveness of wind screens, canopies and trees beyond the single RWDI project (screens at least 1.8 m tall, 20-40% porous), including winter versus summer foliage; no sourced leaf area density values for porous-media tree runs ('City in Nature' planting, link to ECOL).

How Vancouver staff and the Urban Design Panel judge 'adverse microclimate effects' under the Higher Buildings Policy (no numeric rule found); downtown rezoning wind reports were not obtainable in r1 or r2 (HTTP 403), so the accepted criteria family, station, seasons and hours are unknown.

Correct conversion between pedestrian-level (1.5 m) speed and the 10 m wind input of UTCI: the log-law factor (1.38 at 1.5 m, 1.47 at 1.1 m) rests on z0 = 0.01 m and 1.1 m recalled from the UTCI procedure; primary text not opened; validity inside a built canopy unknown.
Effect of neighbouring approved or future towers (named in the brief) on wind at the site, and how a Vancouver review would define the cumulative scenario.
Accuracy of ML surrogates and steady RANS for 244-305 m towers, and for terraces at height; no validation found; AIJ case E has only a 60 m high-rise.
Effect of corner treatment, taper and tower height on structural wind loads and vortex shedding; deferred to P10 (confirm the current Vancouver Building By-law edition first).
Size of the extra sampling scatter that single 1- or 2-minute ECCC means add to exceedance statistics (no mean-level bias expected; scatter not quantified).

Vancouver-specific per-sector roughness, displacement height and gradient height, and internal-boundary-layer development for water-to-city transitions (Burrard Inlet, English Bay, False Creek); ESDU 01008 (named by City of London) was not opened and applicability to Vancouver is unverified.
Effect of atmospheric stability (Arctic outflow, clear nocturnal hours, sea breeze) on the exposure transfer and on neutral-inflow CFD; no sourced proxy thresholds.
Validity of a log-law or Deaves-Harris inflow profile and of the top boundary condition for 244-305 m towers in a domain about 1.8 km high; terraces at 150-300 m.
Normalisation convention of Eddy3D VAF output (the VAF page names no reference; the ABL component defaults to 10 m, 5 m/s, z0 1 m).

Decision-level acceptance bands for CFD validation (class agreement, exceedance bias) and the COST 732/VDI 3783-9 hit rate: primary texts not opened; identity and data access of the AIJ single-tall-building and tall-building-among-low-rise cases unconfirmed.

Whether the AIJ and COST 732 domain rules read second-hand (6 Hmax high, 20 Hmax long, blockage at most 3%) suffice for 305 m towers in dense context, and how blockage is computed with explicit neighbouring towers.
Measured core-hours and cell counts for L2-lite and L2-full runs at 244-305 m scale: only a linear extrapolation from a 0.26 M cell laboratory case (S49) exists.

Which ground-roughness set-up gives better pedestrian-level agreement: a large z0 on the whole ground as in Hagbo (z0 = 3 m, 0.68 m cells) or an atmospheric rough wall upstream with a small z0 on modelled ground; untested here, and the sand-grain relation (Blocken 2007) is recalled.
Anisotropy factor for gusts derived from RANS TKE (surface-layer sigma_u of about 2.4-2.5 u* is recalled) and its validity in wakes.
Cyclist wind criteria beyond the City of London 15 m/s limit (Toronto and Hamilton are silent) and the cycle-route layout implied by the brief.
Ice and snow shedding from a 244-305 m tower onto the public realm and transit plaza: no sourced relationship; hand-off to P10 and SPAC.
Wind- and stack-driven drafts at tower entrances and the below-grade secondary transit connection: no sourced criteria; hand-off to SYST.
Wind-driven rain exposure versus canopy depth, and the Vancouver weather-protection requirements; driving-rain method ISO 15927-3 not opened.
Whether ECCC Vancouver Harbour CS has an hourly wind record of adequate length and exposure.
Concurrent hourly solar for a 30-year record: no co-located series identified; TMYx radiation is a typical year.
Effect of climate change on Vancouver wind and temperature statistics; no future weather files applied.
Governing season for Vancouver pedestrian wind: derive from the M01 wind rose rather than assume.
Number of L2-calibrated massings needed before the M03 composite risk index is meaningful (about 10 is a team placeholder).
change_log: Round 1: Built P03 with 8 modules: wind climate (M01), trigger and criteria selector (M02), massing screening (M03), comfort and safety classifier (M04), CFD and surrogate engine (M05), UTCI (M06), mitigation advisor (M07), elevated terraces (M08).

Round 1: Replaced the assumption 'Vancouver has its own wind criteria' with analog Canadian municipal criteria after no Vancouver numeric criteria could be found or opened; flagged UNVERIFIED and TEAM_ASSUMPTION.
Round 1: Corrected FALSE ASSUMPTIONS: Lawson and RWDI limits are not interchangeable; airport or typical-year wind is not site wind; early CFD cannot certify gust safety; calm is not always better.
Round 1: Priority split: M01-M04 core for the 13 Nov working core and VTC entrants before 30 Nov; M05-M07 v1 by 10 Dec; M08 roadmap.

Lawson metric downgraded to unverified and mean-only.

r2: M01 MAJOR fixed: removed the mean-level averaging-time conversion. ECCC speeds are single sampled 1-, 2- or 10-minute means (2-minute at aviation stations since the late 1980s, per the ECCC technical documentation S53), so they estimate the hourly mean without bias; the sampling period is metadata only and pedestrian gusts come from VAF plus turbulence. Metric renamed 'Sampling period declared, no mean-level conversion' (false_assumption_corrected); FALSE_ASSUMPTION flag added.

r2: M01 MAJOR fixed: the single site roughness is replaced by a per-sector roughness, displacement and fetch table (water versus city sectors), a named transfer model (Deaves-Harris/ESDU 01008 as City of London, or a log law capped at gradient height) and a default reference height of 120 m (City of London convention, at least 100 m).

r2: M01 MAJOR fixed: M01 now emits one WindClimate per time base (concurrent-30y and TMYx), each with a record id, ReferenceSpec and the same per-sector correction; M04 builds a ProbeWindSeries per time base and M06 refuses mismatched tags, so the TMYx default has a consistent wind input.

r2: M01 MINOR fixed: calms (ECCC direction 0, verified in S44 and S53) get their own class instead of the north bin; hours are tagged with an editable stability proxy and the outflow-hour share is reported separately. M01 effort raised from S to M.

r2: M05 MAJOR fixed: ground roughness and wall functions. Approach-flow z0 is separated from a small z0 on explicitly modelled ground; OpenFOAM-12 nutkAtmRoughWallFunction (verified in the source tree, S51) is the atmospheric rough wall function; the z0 = 1 m / 0.3 m cell conflict is documented (sand-grain relation recalled from Blocken 2007, S52 unopened); Hagbo's z0 = 3 m practice is recorded as differing.

r2: M05 MAJOR fixed: the 1.5 m empty-domain test is replaced by a horizontal-homogeneity check of U, k and epsilon at 1.5 m, 10 m, H/2 and H (M04 and M05 metrics, FALSE_ASSUMPTION flag). Inflow profile capped at gradient height with a consistent top boundary condition and a declaration up to at least 1.2 H; OpenFOAM-12 atmBoundaryLayer shown to be an uncapped log law (S50).

r2: M05 MAJOR fixed: compute budget added. notes: Key finding unchanged: no City of Vancouver numeric pedestrian wind-comfort criteria or mandatory trigger could be found or opened. In r1 and r2 every City of Vancouver host (vancouver.ca, guidelines, syc, council, rezoning) returned HTTP 403, and the Shape Your City download links redirect to those hosts, so the downtown rezoning wind reports that would show which criteria staff accept were not obtained; a team member must download two or three by hand and fill the M02 PrecedentTable. The Toronto 2022 default (10/15/20 km/h GEM at 80%, gust 90 km/h at 0.1%) therefore stays an editable team assumption, with Hamilton 2026, RWDI and City Lawson (2.5/4/6/8 m/s on mean and GEM at 5%, safety 15 m/s at 0.022%, 24 h) as separate CriteriaSets. r2 changes: station wind is no longer multiplied by an averaging-time factor (ECCC speeds are sampled means); exposure is corrected per 22.5 degree sector (water versus city fetch) with a named transfer model and a 120 m default reference; M01 emits one WindClimate per time base so the M06 TMYx default has matching wind. M05 now separates approach-flow roughness from ground roughness on modelled terrain, caps the inflow at gradient height with a declared top condition and homogeneity test, states a compute budget (about 57 core-hours per million cells per direction, derived from one reported case) and defines an L2-lite comparative level; validation is by comfort-class agreement and exceedance bias, not dispersion-model bands. Early-stage prediction remains limited: CFD is weak on gusts and safety, steady RANS is biased against tunnels (-1% to -35% in one benchmark), surrogates are unvalidated for supertall towers, and no supertall benchmark exists. Structural wind is handled in P10. Open items: Vancouver policy text and precedents, COST 732/VDI 3783-9/AIJ primary texts, UTCI wind-conversion source, ESDU 01008, ECCC Vancouver Harbour CS wind record.
